Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Cost-price discrepancies were investigated in BUS UAT for test products MC395379T1 and ML351505. MC395379T1 had a manually updated cost price in Bus Price Master Staging that differed from Realtime Staging Master. ML351505 had a NULL Price Group, causing its Realtime Staging Master Cost Price to remain aligned with Bus Price Master Staging; the Price Group was updated and the record reprocessed.
Important Findings: ['For product MC395379T1, the cost price in Bus Price Master Staging was manually updated for testing and differed from Realtime Staging Master.', 'For product ML351505 in BUS UAT, the Price Group was NULL.', 'The NULL Price Group caused the Cost Price in Realtime Staging Master for ML351505 to remain the same as the value in Bus Price Master Staging.', 'The Bus Price Master Staging cost price for MC395379T1 was corrected and the record was reprocessed.', 'The Price Group for ML351505 was updated and the Bus Price Master Staging record was reprocessed.']
Root Cause: Manual cost-price modification in Bus Price Master Staging for MC395379T1 and a NULL Price Group for ML351505 in BUS UAT.
Resolution: Corrected the cost price for MC395379T1 in Bus Price Master Staging and reprocessed the record; updated the Price Group for ML351505 and reprocessed its Bus Price Master Staging record.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Users could not select model codes while creating quotes, stopping quotation operations. Investigation confirmed that the Catalog File was not imported and that the Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order. This left model codes unassociated with the Body Type selected in the quote, preventing their display; recovery was completed and models became selectable.
Important Findings: ['Model codes on the quotation screen are displayed based on the Body Type selected in the quote.', 'The Catalog File was not imported into the system.', 'The Model Code and Catalog files were not executed in the correct order.', 'Because of the incorrect execution order, model codes were not configured with the Body Type selected in the quote.', 'The issue was caused by a work error during the file-loading process.', 'Recovery was completed and models became available for selection.']
Root Cause: The Catalog File was not imported and the Model Code and Catalog files were executed in the wrong order, leaving model codes unassociated with the selected Body Type.
Resolution: Completed recovery by correcting the file-loading/execution process so that models became available for selection; planned automation and streamlining of catalog-file imports as a preventive measure.
Technical Entities: ['Catalog File', 'Model Code', 'Model Code file', 'Body Type', 'quote', 'quotation screen', 'model codes', 'TOB', 'SIEBEL', 'model master']

Resolution: Corrected the headquarters-position mapping in the migrated approval hierarchy, restoring correct approval progression and position-based user assignment.

Issue raised in environment: Common
Impacted Environments : Common
Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Job Cards were assigning incorrect labor price lists for their creation branch. In BUS UAT, Branch Price List selection depends on the Billing Type and a non-blank Discount Classification from the Vehicle/Chassis; otherwise the system defaults to an SC Price List such as FDP B Price List. The price list setup was corrected, and newly created Job Cards correctly selected the applicable Branch Price List; existing Job Cards retained the previously stamped Branch Labor Price List Id.
Important Findings: ['Branch Price List is selected only when Billing Type is an eligible inspection-related value and Discount Classification is populated.', 'Discount Classification is sourced from the Vehicle/Chassis record.', 'When the selection conditions are not met, the system defaults to the SC Price List, including FDP Price List/FDP B Price List.', 'Job Card I050000511 used a Vehicle/Chassis with blank Discount Classification, causing FDP B Price List to be selected.', 'Existing Job Cards created before the price list setup correction retain the old Branch Labor Price List Id, including for newly added labor line items.', 'A newly created Job Card correctly selected Branch GY Price List after the setup update.']
Root Cause: The price list setup contained an incorrect Branch Labor Price List configuration; Job Cards created before the correction had the old/wrong Branch Labor Price List Id stamped on them. Additionally, blank Discount Classification causes the expected fallback to the SC/FDP Price List rather than a Branch Price List.
Resolution: Updated the price list setup and validated that newly created Job Cards select the correct branch-specific price list, including Branch GY Price List. Existing Job Cards must be replaced with newly created Job Cards to use the corrected stamped price list.

Resolution: Corrected the affected master data and configurations to align with SC, removed invalid RecycleFeeMaster value "AB", added all required model codes to Campaign, migrated KitMaster from SC, and fixed VC so all options and corresponding prices display correctly. Root Cause: The TOB D21F file was processed before the corresponding D21A file, so the required Chassis Order and vehicle record did not exist when the Recycle Fee Order creation process ran.
Resolution: The affected record was recovered by re-executing the D21F process after successful completion of the D21A process.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: In FDP, a Quote's Required Quantity could be changed from 3 to 1 after a Sales Order and three child Sales Orders had been created. Although the child Sales Orders were cancelled, the backend retained their linkage to the parent Sales Order, causing Sales Posting to fail. The recommended remediation was to align FDP with SC Production by making Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation; PROD deployment was requested, but completion is not documented.
Important Findings: ['A Required Quantity of 3 created three child Sales Orders during Sales Order approval.', 'After a Quote revision changed Required Quantity from 3 to 1, added options were synchronized to all existing child Sales Orders.', 'Cancelling all child Sales Orders did not remove their backend association with the parent Sales Order, so Sales Posting failed.', 'FDP allowed Required Quantity changes after Sales Order creation, enabling the failing scenario.', 'The proposed FDP behavior is to make Required Quantity read-only after Sales Order creation, matching SC Production.', 'For post-order quantity increases, the proposed process requires cancelling the current Sales Order and creating a new Quote and Sales Order.']
Root Cause: FDP allowed Required Quantity to be reduced after Sales Order creation, but the backend logic did not automatically unlink existing child Sales Orders from the parent Sales Order when Required Quantity became 1.

Root Cause: An invalid Planned Delivery Date of 2007/03/30 in the NV Sales Quote caused the Tax Rate for NV Sales Order SO# A000497806 to remain blank, resulting in NV Sales Order Sheet BIP Report generation failure.
Resolution: A corrected Planned Delivery Date validation fix for NV Sales Quote was tested in FDP UAT-1 and released to all FDP-PRODs on July 10 to prevent invalid date input and resulting blank Tax Rate values.

Root Cause: Concurrent quote-to-Sales Order synchronization and invoice creation updated the same Recycle Fee line item (Line Number = 47, Part# YN5Z), causing Siebel exclusive control to reject the synchronization update.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record. No program correction was required because the incident was a rare concurrent-update scenario and the process was functioning normally afterward.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Recycle Invoice DT27 processing created incorrect Journal Voucher values, initially affecting Segment2 Code fields and later Posting Date and client-code fields. The investigation identified chassis-number derivation/mapping issues, DT27 file formatting sensitivity, and UAT8 mapping differences from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs. The corrected UAT logic was verified with test data, and the fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The calculation and reconciliation process formed the chassis number using "Stamp Code-C#", rather than the chassis-number position highlighted in the DT27 file.', 'Incorrect Segment2 Code(CSJS210) and Segment2 Code(CSJS310) values were initially associated with data received from TOB, including "********************" values in the DT27 Recycle Invoice file.', 'An extra space in the DT27 file caused amount value 80 to be treated as 8 during JV creation.', 'Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) mappings in UAT-8 differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, resulting in incorrect Recycle Invoice JV data.', 'UAT8 master data also caused client-code issues and was updated to match Chugoku prod.', 'After mapping updates, test data verified that JVs were created correctly with the correct Posting Date(CSJS005) and client-code values.']
Root Cause: UAT-8 mappings for Client Code(CSJS208) and Client Code(CSJS308) differed from Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, causing incorrect Recycle Invoice Journal Voucher data. DT27 input formatting, including an extra space that converted 80 to 8, also caused an incorrect JV amount during testing.
Resolution: Updated UAT-8 mappings and master data based on Chugoku prod and other FDP UATs, corrected DT27 test-file formatting, and verified correct Journal Voucher creation with new test data. The approved fix was scheduled for the 2026-07-23 FDP release.

Investigation Summary: Three affected materials caused the Realtime Price Master process to halt because their Product Release batch executions had not completed successfully. The Realtime Price batch validation treated the unreleased materials as invalid master-data entries. The affected production records were recovered and the materials were successfully released; no Siebel fix was required.

Root Cause: The Product Release batch was not completed successfully for three materials, leaving the products unreleased and causing the Realtime Price Master process to reject them as invalid master-data entries.
Resolution: Recovered the affected records in the production environment and successfully released the three materials. No Siebel fix was required.

Investigation Summary: “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS” and “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI” JVs were missing for Body orders because POs for newly added Body line items were created only after Sales Posting had completed. Recovery was completed for the orders listed in the Jira, and additional records with POs created after Sales Posting were identified for review. The current system cannot create the requested Body GI JV after Sales Posting; a permanent enhancement requires new Body Building Order logic and must be handled through PJ-CR.
Important Findings: ['An NV Quotation revision added Body line items and synchronized them to the Sales Order, but POs were not created for all Body-tab line items before Sales Posting.', 'Sales Posting created JVs only for the Sales Order and POs mapped at the time of Sales Posting; remaining POs were created afterward.', '“Sales Posting Body GI” and “Sales Posting Body” JVs are created only during Sales Order Sales Posting and are not generated retrospectively for POs created afterward.', 'The existing “Revised Sales Posting” Journal Event Type creates delta-value JVs for post-Sales-Posting PO creation, but does not provide the requested Body GI JV behavior.', 'Supporting post-Sales-Posting creation of Body GI JVs requires changes to multiple objects and testing of Body Building Order processes and related interfaces.', 'Recovery was completed for the Jira-listed orders, and records with POs created after Sales Posting were shared for review.']
Root Cause: POs for Body line items added through an NV Quotation revision were not created before Sales Posting. When the remaining POs were created after Sales Posting, the system did not create “Sales Posting Body Non IBOS GI” JVs because those JVs are generated only at Sales Order Sales Posting.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders listed in the Jira using recovery JV data linked to KB in the nightly daily batch. A permanent post-Sales-Posting Body GI JV enhancement remains pending and requires PJ-CR.

Resolution: Recovery was completed by setting the Activity status to Work Completed. No fix was required; for canceled Job Cards, users must manually set the linked Activity status to Cancel Request.

Investigation Summary: In UAT1, spreadsheet 1-502819545 appeared not to send an approval request after recovery in SR# 5709, although a pending request remained in the approver's Inbox. Recovery changed the spreadsheet from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed its approval history without removing the associated Inbox request entity. When the approver approved the remaining request, the spreadsheet changed to Spreadsheet Approved; JVs were created for the affected Job Cards. The system was determined to be behaving as expected, and the recovery procedure will be updated to deactivate pending approval requests during recovery.
Important Findings: ['Recovery in SR# 5709 changed the spreadsheet status from Spreadsheet Requested to Spreadsheet Created and removed approval history.', "The request entity remained in the designated approver's Inbox after approval history was removed.", 'A subsequent approval submission did not create approval history, creating the appearance that no approval request had been sent.', 'Approving the remaining Inbox request changed spreadsheet 1-502819545 in UAT1 to Spreadsheet Approved.', 'JVs were created for 37 Job Cards associated with the Insurance Spreadsheet, totaling 148 Journal Voucher Items.', 'Future recovery procedures must deactivate pending approval requests to prevent hidden approvals.']
Root Cause: The recovery performed in SR# 5709 removed the spreadsheet approval history but did not remove the pending approval request entity from the approver's Inbox, disrupting the normal approval-history flow.
Resolution: Created JVs for the 37 affected Job Cards (148 Journal Voucher Items) and updated the recovery procedure requirement to deactivate pending approval requests to designated approvers during spreadsheet recovery.

Root Cause: The existing 'Create Activity' button logic disabled the button after creating one Activity for all Service Effort line items, without allowing another Activity based on the status of the previous JCO.
Resolution: Updated the UV Sales Order logic to enable creation of a second Activity when the previous JCO is Closed or Cancelled; tested in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to production.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A TOB chassis invoice record in DT01 for C#: FP84HG-500043 did not create a Journal Voucher (JV). The record resulted in a NULL line type/product type because the relevant product-type field was NULL and Siebel did not have logic to create a JV for that condition. Subsequent analysis also found that the invoice line had no matching Chassis Order Line Item, causing the default Project Code AA00000000 rather than a chassis order number. Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions.
Important Findings: ['The affected record was FP84HG-500043 in the DT01 Chassis Invoice file for the Okayama FDP environment.', 'The billing-data type is identified from the 25th character; the affected record was identified as Post-OP.', 'For the Post-OP record, the 2-character product-type value after the 66th character was NULL, causing the line type/product type to be NULL.', 'Siebel did not contain logic to create a JV when the line type was NULL, so no JV was created.', 'The corresponding invoice data did not exist in the Chassis Order Line Items, although it existed in an associated Sales Order line item; therefore reconciliation could not set the Chassis Order Number as Project Code (CSJS211).', 'When no matching Chassis Order Line Item is found, AA00000000 is assigned as the default project code; manual recovery was confirmed to process all TOB invoices without omission.']
Root Cause: The DT01 Post-OP invoice record had a NULL product-type field, which produced a NULL line type; Siebel had no JV-creation logic for records with a NULL line type. The related invoice line also had no matching Chassis Order Line Item for reconciliation.
Resolution: Manual recovery was validated to process all TOB invoice scenarios without omissions. Future TOB invoice processing will be monitored, and a JV will be created manually when a DT01 record does not produce a JV.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident involved an error when requesting acceptance inspection approval in FDP. Investigation identified that the Approval Master Data did not contain all required requester positions/UIDs; the master was updated in UAT-1 and deployed to Production in the 11 June FDP release.
Important Findings: ['FDP approval requests are permitted only for UIDs maintained as valid requestors in the master data.', 'Users not listed as valid requestors receive the error message "Please select a valid approver" when generating an approval request.', 'The existing master was compared with positions provided by Shiromoto San, and missing positions were added.', 'The updated Approval Master Data included existing requestors and newly added requestors.', 'The fix was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to Production.']
Root Cause: Required requester positions/UIDs were missing from the Approval Master Data, causing FDP approval requests from those users to be rejected as invalid.
Resolution: Updated the Approval Master Data/Multiple_UID_Master with the missing requester positions and valid UIDs, validated the change in UAT-1, and deployed it to Production in the 11 June FDP release.

Earlier logic derived Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position, which could return the wrong branch manager when the creator moved between branches. The logic was revised in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, then deployed to Production through the June 2 emergency release.
Important Findings: ['The initial BIP mapping for Branch Sales Manager name was incorrect.', "The prior BIP logic displayed the Last Name of the Sales Rep's Parent Position as Manager Name.", "The required logic is to display the Branch-Head of the branch from which the quotation originated, rather than the quotation creator's current branch or position hierarchy.", 'Using the creator/Sales Rep as the reference could display a different branch manager when the creator moved from branch A to branch B.', 'After the Production deployment, BIP displays blank when no branch manager exists in the target organization hierarchy.']
Root Cause: Incorrect Sales Quotation BIP mapping logic derived Branch Manager Name from the Sales Rep/creator's parent position instead of the branch associated with the quotation.
Resolution: Changed the BIP logic to display the Branch-Head of the quotation's originating branch, validated the change in FDP UAT-1 and FDP UAT-4, and deployed it to Production via the June 2 emergency release.

Investigation Summary: An error screen occurred when users clicked an approval notification email link after the related approval request had already been approved from the inbox. The approval request was moved to the "Completed Items List", while the email URL continued to reference the original pending request. The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and confirmed as expected system behavior; the incident was closed.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurs when an approval request is approved directly from the inbox before the notification email link is opened.', 'Approved requests are automatically moved from the inbox pending list to the "Completed Items List".', 'The notification email URL still references the original pending approval request after approval.', 'Opening the stale email URL after approval results in the error screen.', 'The behavior was replicated in UAT1 and determined not to be a bug.']
Root Cause: The notification email link references a pending approval request that is no longer available after the request has been approved and moved to the "Completed Items List".
Resolution: Confirmed the behavior as expected system behavior, rejected the incident, and closed it.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: D/N prices were not reflected across FDPs because D2S price master files contained Cost Price but omitted list price, and the old package therefore did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List. The Bulk Price batch was scheduled on Production for all FDPs and its execution times were adjusted so price updates complete before 07:00 JST.
Important Findings: ['D2S price master files contained Cost Price but were missing list price.', 'The old package did not set D/N price in PT_Price_List when list price was absent.', 'Recovery completed and D/N prices were reflected across all FDPs for the affected part numbers.', 'Bulk Price batch was scheduled for all FDPs on Production to process price files received from D2S.', 'Job timings were changed to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST so updates complete before 07:00 JST.', 'Price updates were confirmed as working correctly on all FDPs, including FDP-OKAYAMA.']
Root Cause: Price master files received from D2S omitted list price; during execution of the old package, this prevented D/N price from being set in PT_Price_List.
Resolution: Completed recovery, scheduled the Bulk Price batch for all FDPs on Production, and adjusted job timings to 04:30 JST and 05:00 JST to complete price updates before 07:00 JST.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: BIP reports generated through the Siebel "Submit" button included only the selected order line when a user selected a specific line item. This was identified as standard behavior of the vanilla BIP; selecting the Sales Order Header before submission included all line items. The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 and the changes were deployed to Production on April 07 after business hours.
Important Findings: ['The Siebel standard (vanilla) BIP invoked through the "Submit" button cannot be modified.', 'When a specific order line item is selected, the "Submit" BIP report includes only that selected line item.', 'Selecting the Sales Order Header before using "Submit" causes the BIP report to include all line items.', 'The custom BIP accessed through the "Generate" button was provided as an alternative to avoid the line-item selection behavior.', 'The same behavior was observed in the SC UAT-1 environment for Reference Order #: A027129251.', 'The issue was fixed in FDP UAT-1 for NV Sales Order#: A001297322 and A001256624, then deployed to Production.']
Root Cause: The standard Siebel vanilla BIP generated through the "Submit" button scopes the report to the selected order line item when a line is selected.
Resolution: Changes were validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to the Production environment on April 07 after business hours; users were advised to use the custom "Generate" BIP or select the Sales Order Header before using "Submit".

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Duplicate chassis orders and pool cost orders were created when the same D21A chassis information was processed before and after its model code became available in master data. D21A_19112025200850 (TOB) created chassis order B000303862 without model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 because the code was absent from master data; after TCH01 created the code, D21A_17122025200816 (TOB) created B000332117 with the model code. The behavior matches the current system design, but a permanent corrective measure was not agreed or completed.
Important Findings: ['D21A processing created a chassis order even when the received model code was not present in system master data.', 'Model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was created by TCH01 on 17 December 2025 after a business request, rather than through normal daily file processing.', 'When the same chassis information was re-received through D21A after the model code became available, the system created a new chassis order instead of updating the existing order.', 'The duplicate chassis orders resulted in duplicate pool cost orders.', 'The requested automatic upsert of a newly available model code to an existing chassis order is not possible within the current D21A/Siebel design because D21A creates both vehicle data and chassis order data and changes may affect dependent systems and business processes.', 'Including MC-9 model codes in daily TCH01 processing was proposed as a future prevention option, but it was rejected as not being a solution.']
Root Cause: The model code MS06GPQGUCV-9 was unavailable in system master data during the initial D21A processing, so the system created a chassis order without the model code. After TCH01 created the model code, re-receipt of the same D21A information was processed as a new chassis order rather than an update, causing duplicate chassis and pool cost orders.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Sales Order A050609736 was not synchronized to the latest Quote Revision and remained at revision 2. Error monitoring showed that the Sales Order synchronization failed because an order line record was modified by another user/session after retrieval. The affected record was recovered; no product fix was required because the process was functioning normally, including in UAT.
Important Findings: ["The failure occurred in step 'Sync Sales Order' using service 'EAI Siebel Adapter' and method 'Synchronize' (SBL-BPR-00162).", "'WriteRecord' for business component 'MF RF Order Entry - Line Items' and integration component 'MF Order Item' returned SBL-DAT-00523 and SBL-EAI-04451.", 'Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 with Total List Price ¥57,100 was being updated from another browser tab or session during Quote-to-Sales-Order synchronization.', 'The concurrent modification prevented the Sales Order from being synchronized to the latest Quote Revision.', 'Recovery was completed for the affected Sales Order record; no fix was required.']
Root Cause: Concurrent modification of the Accessories line item Part#: QZ034500 from another browser tab or session while the user synchronized the quote to the Sales Order caused a record-lock/concurrency error (SBL-DAT-00523), leaving Sales Order A050609736 at revision 2.
Resolution: Recovered the affected Sales Order record. No product fix was implemented because the issue was attributed to rare simultaneous user operations and the process was operating normally.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident involved inconsistent behavior when setting the "Bill to Basic Account Code" field in Siebel. Analysis identified missing explicit sequencing of field-value setting, similar to a prior issue involving "Bill to Basic Account Name". The sequencing fix was implemented at the Business Component level, validated in UAT, and released to production on the 23rd.
Important Findings: ['AR and AP Account Ids depend on the User Account Id being set first.', 'Incorrect field-value setting order previously caused failures when fetching AR and AP Account Ids for "Bill to Basic Account Name".', 'The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field did not have equivalent explicit sequence handling and was identified as the cause of inconsistent results.', 'The fix was implemented at the Business Component level, covering MF Job Card Detail Applet, MF JC List Applet (@JC), and MF Job Card List Applet (@Vehicle Master).', 'MF JC Change Order Payment Form Applet (@Change Order) already had the required sequencing and required no change.', 'The change was deployed to all FDP-PRODs and applied to the production environment in the release on the 23rd.']
Root Cause: The "Bill to Basic Account Code" field lacked explicit sequencing to set the User Account Id before retrieving dependent AR and AP Account Ids, resulting in inconsistent behavior.
Resolution: Implemented the required field-value sequencing at the Business Component level, tested it in UAT, and deployed the change to all FDP-PRODs.

Investigation Summary: Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Planned Delivery Date in the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order. This caused an incorrect invoice payment date when the Quote and Sales Order planned delivery dates differed. The mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation was changed to use the Sales Order and was validated in UAT-1 before deployment to PROD in the May 13 release.
Important Findings: ['The affected invoice showed PaymentDueDate 2026-03-31 because Payment Term was 1 and the Quote Planned Delivery Date was 2026-02-25.', 'As an immediate recovery, the Quote Planned Delivery Date was updated to 2026-03-17, matching the Sales Order date, and the invoice displayed the correct value after regeneration.', 'The confirmed defect was that Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate/Planned Payment Date was sourced from NV Quote rather than NV Sales Order.', 'UAT1 tests confirmed that when the Sales Order Planned Delivery Date was present, PaymentDueDate was calculated from the Sales Order date; the test response was sent to KB for invoice report generation.', 'Holiday handling was clarified to include Saturdays, Sundays, and defined public holidays; adding holiday-aware Planned Payment Date calculation was identified as a separate Project Change Request requirement.', 'The mapping fix was released to PROD in the May 13 release.']
Root Cause: The Planned Delivery Date used to calculate Individual Invoice PaymentDueDate was mapped from the Quote/NV Quote instead of the Sales Order/NV Sales Order.
Resolution: Updated the Planned Delivery Date mapping for Planned Payment Date calculation from Sales Quote/NV Quote to Sales Order/NV Sales Order, validated the change in UAT-1, and released it to PROD on May 13.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Duplicate vehicle records were created when a vehicle was initially registered without a model code because the model code was unavailable in the Production environment. After the model code was added, the update process searched by model code and could not match the original record, so it created a new record. Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles were recovered, and monitoring was deployed across all FDP environments to detect and recover similar records promptly.
Important Findings: ['The initial vehicle record was created without a model code because the code was not available in the Production environment.', 'The update process uses the model code to locate an existing vehicle record.', 'Because the original record lacked the model code, the system could not identify it and created a duplicate vehicle record with the correct model code.', 'Example impacted record: Hakodate Production vehicle MS06GP-20085; initial record created on 19 Dec 2025, model code added on 23 Dec 2025 under SR MFTBCFFR-5162, and duplicate creation occurred during the 24 Dec 2025 update.', 'Impacted Sales Orders and vehicles required recovery; recovery of the Hakodate vehicle was completed.', 'A monitoring script was deployed across all FDP environments to send email alerts for similar records so they can be recovered immediately.']
Root Cause: The model code was unavailable when the original vehicle record was created, leaving that record without a model code. After the code was added, the system's model-code-based update lookup could not find the original record and created a duplicate vehicle record.
Resolution: Recovered impacted Sales Orders and vehicle records, and deployed a monitoring script across all FDP environments that sends email alerts for records matching this condition, enabling immediate recovery.

Root Cause: When Payment Date was null in NV Sales Order and NV Quote, the Invoice logic did not derive a payment date from the required delivery-related dates and payment-deadline conditions.
Resolution: Implemented the corrected payment-date derivation logic based on user feedback, completed UAT-1 testing, and released the change to PROD in the 13th May release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Sales Orders were displayed in the logged-in user's 'My' view even when the user was not the sales person in charge. Investigation determined that visibility was granted to all members listed in the Other Team Members/Sales Order team context. The visibility logic was changed so that only the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association can view the order in 'My'; the change was deployed to Production on 23/04/2026.
Important Findings: ['Entity Transfer added users to the Sales Order team, causing multiple users to be associated with an order.', "The issue occurred because Sales Orders were visible in 'My' view for all members shown in the Other Team Members applet.", "The required behavior was that selecting 'My' must not display orders belonging to other sales representatives.", 'The final visibility rule uses the logged-in user as the Primary Employee of the primary position association with the order.', 'The same correction was applied to the NV Quotes tab.', 'The production deployment was completed in the release on 23/04/2026.']
Root Cause: The 'My' view visibility logic allowed all users associated through the Other Team Members/Sales Order team to view a Sales Order, instead of restricting visibility to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association.
Resolution: Implemented code-level visibility logic restricting Sales Order and NV Quotes tab 'My' view results to the logged-in user who is the Primary Employee of the order's primary position association, then deployed the fix to Production on 23/04/2026.

Important Findings: ['The incorrect value "Y" in "Profit Amount High Flag" caused the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to be triggered incorrectly.', '"Profit Amount High Flag" is a backend field used in approval-flow conditions for NV Quote revisions based on Sales Profit changes.', 'For revised NV Quotes, the flag should be "Y" when Sales Profit remains the same or increases, and "N" when Sales Profit decreases.', 'The issue was replicated in FDP UAT-1 using multi-browsing activity; other tested approval-flow cases were reported as working correctly.', 'The implemented fix recalculates "Profit Amount High Flag" based on the latest updates made during Quote revision.', 'The fix was deployed to Production through the FDP release on April 23.']
Root Cause: During NV Quote revision, "Profit Amount High Flag" was incorrectly updated to "Y" due to multi-browsing activity, causing the "FDP Operating Profit Quote Change" approval flow to trigger instead of the applicable flow.
Resolution: Implemented a code-level fix to recalculate "Profit Amount High Flag" using the latest Quote revision updates, validated the NV Quote approval process in FDP UAT-1, and deployed the change to Production in the April 23 FDP release.

Investigation Summary: A delivery approval error occurred for an NV Sales Order after the associated Chassis Order was moved to "Pending" through an SR and then reprocessed to "Ordered." The system attempted to create another Vehicle record; because a Vehicle already existed, the existing Vehicle was unmapped from the Chassis Order and Sales Order. Important Findings: ['Approving an NV Sales Order with Product Class "Trailer" automatically created a Chassis Order.', 'Setting the Chassis Order to "Ordered" created a Vehicle that was mapped to both the Chassis Order and Sales Order.', 'After the Chassis Order was set to "Pending" through an SR and reprocessed to "Ordered," the system attempted to create a new Vehicle record.', 'Because a Vehicle record already existed, no new Vehicle was created and the existing Vehicle was unmapped from both related orders.', 'The behavior was replicated in UAT-1 using SO# A001302411 and Chassis Order# B001302412.']
Root Cause: Recovery performed under an SR changed the Chassis Order status to "Pending" after a Vehicle had already been created. Reprocessing the order to "Ordered" caused the system to attempt Vehicle creation and unmap the existing Vehicle from the Chassis Order and Sales Order.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record on February 27; the user successfully completed Sales Posting for the Sales Order.

Investigation Summary: In NV FDP China, trade-in vehicles were not displayed on the Sales Order Sheet, and Stamped Model Code, Registered Year, and C/# number were blank in NV quotations and sales orders. Investigation confirmed that Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0, while Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are sourced from the Product ID of the linked Model Code. The observed values were blank in FDP production and SC production; C/# number is designed to remain blank in both environments.
Important Findings: ['Order Sheet BIP displays trade-in items only when Trade-In Amount is greater than 0.', 'The target NV quotation had Trade-In Amount set to 0 on the trade-in vehicle detail line, so the trade-in item was not displayed.', 'Registered Year and Stamped Model Code are populated from the Product ID of the linked Model Code.', 'The applicable Model Code had blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code values in both FDP production and SC production.', 'C/# number is always blank by design in both SC and FDP environments.', 'SC production SO# A037817024 also had Trade-In Amount of 0 and therefore did not display the trade-in item in Order Sheet BIP.']
Root Cause: The trade-in vehicle was not displayed because its Trade-In Amount was 0, which does not meet the Order Sheet BIP condition of Trade-In Amount greater than 0. Blank Registered Year and Stamped Model Code resulted from blank values on the applicable linked Model Code; C/# number is blank by design.
Resolution: No corrective change was applied. The behavior was confirmed as existing Order Sheet BIP logic and existing data/configuration; updating C/# number was offered if requested.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: An Assessment Request for an Unstock Vehicle could not be updated to "Completed" because it became read-only after reaching "Vehicle for Quotation". The request was created by user D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role, for which existing functionality permits editing only specific statuses. Recovery was completed on February 3 by updating the Assessment Request to "Cancelled", and a logic change was planned for UAT to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable.
Important Findings: ['The Assessment Request was created by user ID D8HIHARA with the Branch-Sales-Staff role.', 'The "Quotation Vehicle Allocation" flag was set to "Y", causing the request to be treated as an Unstock Vehicle case.', 'For Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff, statuses outside the configured editable-status list are read-only.', 'When the request status became "Vehicle for Quotation", UV staff could not update it to "Completed" because the status was read-only.', 'A review of the FDP production environment found no other similar incidents.']
Root Cause: Existing editability logic made Assessment Requests created by Branch-Sales-Staff read-only when their status was set to "Vehicle for Quotation", preventing UV staff from changing the status to "Completed".
Resolution: On February 3, the affected Assessment Request status was updated to "Cancelled". A follow-up change was planned in the UAT environment to keep "Vehicle for Quotation" editable even when the request was created by Branch-Sales-Staff.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: UV Sales Quote profit calculation mismatched for production record AR#: H000522508, Quote#: 2-AJ8LJK, an Unstock Vehicle case. A blank Vehicle ID on the Model Code line item caused it to be classified as a Non-Vehicle Line Item and its price to be deducted twice. The affected record was recovered, and the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification was corrected, validated in UAT1, and released to Production on February 19.
Important Findings: ['The affected record was an Unstock Vehicle, where the chassis number was not mapped to the assessment.', 'Vehicle and Non-Vehicle line item prices in UV Sales Quote are calculated separately based on the Vehicle ID in the Model Code line item.', 'For Unstock Vehicle cases, the Model Code line item has no chassis and its Vehicle ID remains blank.', 'The blank Vehicle ID caused the Model Code line item to be treated as a Non-Vehicle Line Item, resulting in its price being deducted twice during Sales Profit calculation.', "The corrected Non-Vehicle Line Item search condition identifies records with blank Vehicle ID only when Product Type is not 'Model Code'.", 'The fix was implemented in UAT1 using AR#: H000052299 and UV Quote#: 1-7WLRVD, then released to Production on February 19.']
Root Cause: For an Unstock Vehicle, the Model Code line item had a blank Vehicle ID because no chassis was present. The Non-Vehicle Line Item search logic therefore misclassified the Model Code line item as non-vehicle, causing the Model Code price to be deducted twice during UV Sales Quote profit calculation.
Resolution: Recovered the affected record and updated the Non-Vehicle Line Item search specification to exclude records with Product Type 'Model Code' when Vehicle ID is blank. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Production on February 19.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A Tax amount finalization error was replicated in UAT-1 using UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882. The issue occurred after a user manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax'; the affected YN6M line item was not updated to Invoiced when the invoice was created. The incident was classified as user misoperation, with no affected cases found in any FDP Production Environment; users should revise the UV Sales Quote and restore the correct expense line items.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT-1 with UV Sales Quote 1-6XPN5P revision 5 and UV Sales Order E001300882.', "Creating an invoice automatically updates standard line items with Type 'Tax' to status Invoiced.", "The manually changed line item with Part Number YN6M and Type 'Tax' was not updated to Invoiced.", "Tax Finalization requires all line items with Type 'Tax', including manually updated lines, to be Invoiced.", "No cases of manually changing an Expense Line item to 'Tax' were found in any FDP Production Environment."]
Root Cause: User manually changed an Expense Item to Type 'Tax', causing the YN6M line item to remain outside the expected invoicing-status update and not be set to Invoiced before Tax Finalization.
Resolution: No system fix or recovery was required. The user should revise the UV Sales Quote and update the correct expense line items.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The issue was reproduced for JC# I001300905 on FDP - UAT1: a Quote Item showed Line Discount % as 0% after manually entering List Unit Price for Dummy Lubricant (..999999), while the synced JCO Order Item showed 100%. Investigation identified differing Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item, associated with a null Lubrication Price. A JCO-side fix was implemented in UAT and deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated on FDP - UAT1 for JC# I001300905.', 'When List Unit Price was manually entered for Dummy Lubricant (..999999) while the Quote was In Progress, Quote Item Line Discount % was 0%.', 'After the Quote became Customer Approved and the JCO was created/synced, the Order Item Line Discount % became 100%.', 'Quote Item and Order Item used different Line Discount % calculation behavior.', 'The issue was associated with Lubrication Price being null.', 'The initially proposed approach to make List Unit Price read-only was rejected; the fix was changed on the JCO side.']
Root Cause: Different Line Discount % calculation behavior between Quote Item and Order Item when Lubrication Price was null caused the JCO Order Item Line Discount % to become 100% while the Quote Item remained 0%.
Resolution: A JCO-side fix was implemented and validated in UAT, then deployed to PROD in the January 22 regular release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Chassis Orders were created with a blank/missing model code because the relevant model code was not registered when the TOB/D21A processing occurred. The model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025 after the chassis order had been created on 10-Dec-2025. Impacted records were recovered after model-code creation was restored across FDP environments; the investigation also identified that not all TOB master files are automatically updated.
Important Findings: ['The affected chassis order was created on 10-Dec-2025, while model code "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created on 15-Dec-2025.', 'Model code "MS06GPQUCV-9" was missing from the Chugoku, Wakayama, and Okayama Model Master, preventing chassis-order creation in those environments.', 'Affected Chassis Orders were recovered by correcting master data and reprocessing the relevant records; recovery was reported complete for all impacted records.', 'Model codes with MC "9" were manually updated in Chugoku and Wakayama on 26-Dec-2025 after receipt of the required TCH01 file.', 'TCH01 is the TOB PC Master 2 - Model Master inbound batch interface to Siebel via SFTP and is scheduled as a daily package run in Siebel PROD; not all TOB master interfaces are scheduled for daily PROD processing.', 'The proposed preventive control is to prevent Chassis Order creation when a model code is absent, notify the AMS team by email, correct data, and reprocess the record.']
Root Cause: The required model code was not registered in the system when the TOB/D21A file was processed. Specifically, "MS06GPHZMAV-9" was created after the corresponding Chassis Order, and TOB master updates were not configured so that all master files were automatically updated.
Resolution: Model-code creation was restored and missing model codes were manually updated in the affected FDP environments. The impacted Chassis Orders were recovered and reprocessed after the required master data was available.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The reported amount mismatch between the order form and sales estimate was initially observed as different discount mappings between Quotation BIP and Order Sheet BIP. The final investigation determined that the Quote price was changed after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approval, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order. This was classified as a user mis-operation rather than a product defect.
Important Findings: ['Quotation BIP showed a Discount amount of -819798 from MF Vehicle Discount Amount, while Order Sheet BIP showed -60000 from MF UV Discount.', 'The Quote price was changed after the Quote had been approved and the Sales Order had been created.', 'A price change made after Quote approval without re-approval is not reflected in the Sales Order.', 'The incident was determined not to be a bug and was proposed for rejection.']
Root Cause: The user changed the Quote price after Quote approval and Sales Order creation without re-approving the Quote, so the updated price was not reflected in the Sales Order.
Resolution: Users should avoid changing the Price after Quote Approval; the incident was rejected as a user mis-operation rather than a bug.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation compared the entered Branch Code with the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, preventing invoicing when the codes differed. For I000111578 (D8YOOSEK), the relevant Primary Location Code was "70"; for I000111572 (D8MICSAS), it was "00". CR MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code filter, allowing Individual Invoice issuance from Branch Code "00"; Bulk Invoice was unaffected because it selects Branch from the JC Header.
Important Findings: ["The entered Branch Code was validated against the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, which can be checked in the employee Location Code.", 'I000111578 (D8YOOSEK) had Primary Location Code "70", while I000111572 (D8MICSAS) had Primary Location Code "00".', 'Before the MFTBCFFR-4379 release, I000111578 could be invoiced using Branch Code "70".', 'MFTBCFFR-4379 removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice, allowing invoice issuance from Branch Code "00".', 'Bulk Invoice was not affected because Branch is selected from the JC Header.']
Root Cause: Individual Invoice Branch Code validation/filter required the entered Branch Code to match the JCO creator's Primary Location Code, causing failures when the codes differed.
Resolution: Deployed CR MFTBCFFR-4379, which removed the Branch Code validation/filter for Individual Invoice.

Investigation Summary: The Expense Invoice BIP report displayed the value from "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)". The issue affected all FDP Production environments and resulted from a required BIP report update not being completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625. Important Findings: ['Expense Invoice BIP report used "Integrated Address(J)" rather than "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" for the address value.', 'For Invoice 1-130032159 and Account 0C00240272, the report was corrected to display "1-4-11 Minami-Shinozakicho, Edogawa-ku, Tokyo".', 'The issue was not specific to Chugoku; it existed in all FDP Production environments.', 'A necessary BIP report update was missed after code changes related to MFTBCFFR-4625.', 'The corrected address display was validated in UAT before production approval.']
Root Cause: A required BIP report update was not completed after the code changes associated with MFTBCFFR-4625, causing Expense Invoice BIP to map the address to "Integrated Address(J)" instead of "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)".
Resolution: Updated the Expense Invoice BIP report to display the correct "Address(J) character-chome(Vender)" value, validated the change in UAT, and deployed it in the 17th Dec FDP release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Delivery Approval failed for NV Sales Order records A000009087 and A000011464 in the Wakayama Production environment. The failure was traced to a Vehicle ID mismatch between the automatically created Purchase Order and its corresponding Sales Order. The affected records were recovered, but the underlying reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined because required historical system information was no longer retained.
Important Findings: ['Both affected NV Sales Orders had product class "Trailer", which automatically creates a "Trailer & Forklift" Purchase Order after Sales Order approval.', 'When the Purchase Order status changed to "Ordered", a new Vehicle record was created and its Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order.', 'Delivery Approval validates Vehicle information between the Purchase Order and Sales Order; the Vehicle ID mismatch caused the validation error and blocked Delivery Approval.', 'The issue could not be reproduced in UAT or FDP UAT, and no similar recurrence was observed in production environments during subsequent monitoring.', 'The affected Purchase Orders were processed in March 2025 but the incident was reported in December 2025, after the required system-information retention period had expired.', 'System log retention is planned to be extended from one month to two months to support investigation of future occurrences reported within the retention period.']
Root Cause: The immediate cause of the Delivery Approval error was a Vehicle ID mismatch: the newly created Vehicle ID was populated on the Purchase Order but not on the corresponding Sales Order. The reason the Vehicle ID was not populated on the Sales Order could not be determined.
Resolution: Affected records were recovered. No defect was identified in the current implementation and no reproducible code fix was confirmed; continued monitoring and extension of system log retention from one month to two months were planned for future investigation and recurrence prevention.

Resolution: Changed the JV Base Amount mapping to Purchase Order Total price on UAT1, validated the change, and released it to Prod in the 17th Dec FDP release. Recovery required reverse and corrected JVs for affected BB orders with posting date 20251211.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: When changing the Sales Rep on a Sales Order, the Entity Transfer functionality did not initially display D8OKATAR because the Employee Applet search logic required the same Primary Position Type as the current Sales Rep. Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition allowed users from other locations to appear. The search logic was corrected to display only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code, and the fix was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The original Entity Transfer condition required users to be in the same organization and have the same Primary Position Type as the primary Sales Rep.', 'D8OKATAR was excluded because its Primary Position Type was Branch-Sales-Staff, while D8TAKOUN and D8THORIK had Branch-Sales-Manager.', 'The Primary Position Type condition had been added under MFTBCFFR-4341, but the requested behavior was branch-based selection without a job/position-type restriction.', "Removing the Sales Rep Primary position Id condition made positions in the Sales Rep's department visible, but also displayed users from other locations.", "The Employee Applet search logic was revised so Entity Transfer displays users with the same branch as the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code."]
Root Cause: The Employee Applet/Entity Transfer search logic used a Sales Rep Primary Position Type condition rather than limiting eligible users solely by the Sales Order branch; after that condition was removed, the logic was still insufficiently constrained and displayed users from other locations.
Resolution: Corrected the Employee Applet search logic to show only users whose branch matches the Sales Order's Branch 2 Digit Code. The change was released in the 17th Dec FDP release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: After SO Sales Posting, revising an NV/UV Quote to change the Customer Account created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV and omitted the Consumption Tax JV. The issue was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093. The logic was updated and validated on UAT1, then deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred when an NV/UV Quote was revised after SO Sales Posting and the Customer Account changed without a Sales Amount change.', "Existing logic created revised Journal Voucher items only when the Sales Amount changed; otherwise, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.", 'The missing Consumption Tax JV was reproduced on UAT1 for SO # A001299134 and A001299093.', 'The same functionality and affected logic apply to UV and across all FDPs.', 'Past JVs have been affected because the logic has existed since FDP go-live.']
Root Cause: Existing revised Journal Voucher logic created Consumption Tax Journal entries only for Journal Voucher items with a Sales Amount change. When only the Customer Account or other non-amount values changed, it created only the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' JV.
Resolution: Updated the logic to create the Consumption Tax Journal together with the 'Revise Sales Posting Selling' Journal even when the Sales Amount is unchanged and fields such as Customer Account change. The fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to FDP Production in the 26th November planned release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee order/line items were created when the D21A ODI package processed a TOB file whose Model Code did not match the Model Code stored in the Vehicle record. The affected data was recovered in production, including JV recovery and cancellation of duplicate Chassis Order B050481404. The evidence did not conclusively establish that a user changed the Model Code through the Administration Vehicle screen. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version and proposed for FDP after approval.
Important Findings: ['Chassis Order B050208984 and its Vehicle record were initially created with Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830; the Vehicle record later contained FBA20B21W00F-4-G830.', 'A TOB D21A file received on 7 November 2025 contained Model Code FBA20B21W00F-5-G830.', 'Because the D21A ODI package did not match the incoming Model Code to the Vehicle record, it treated the data as new and created duplicate Chassis Order B050481404, a new Vehicle, and duplicate recycle fee order and line items.', 'JV recovery was completed and the duplicate order was cancelled in the production environment; recycle fee attributes became visible after recovery.', 'The claimed user mis-operation through the Administration Vehicle screen was disputed and was not proven by the recorded last-updated user or replication results.', 'The SC-version fix matches the TOB Model Code against the Chassis Order Line Item rather than the Vehicle record and updates the Vehicle Model Code from TOB; equivalent FDP implementation was pending approval.']
Root Cause: A Model Code mismatch between the incoming TOB D21A file/original Chassis Order Line Item (FBA20B21W00F-5-G830) and the Vehicle record (FBA20B21W00F-4-G830) caused the D21A ODI package to identify the data as new and create duplicate Vehicle, Chassis Order, and recycle fee records.
Resolution: Completed JV recovery and cancelled duplicate Chassis Order B050481404 in production. A preventive fix was implemented in the SC version under INC6267864 and INC6273871; FDP implementation was proposed pending approval.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Bulk Invoice records for multiple shipments were missing from month-end closing files sent to KB, requiring recovery data to be manually created and transmitted. Investigation found that the post-extraction SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag by order number instead of shipment, causing all shipments under an order to be marked as sent when only one shipment was processed. The SQL was corrected in all production environments, impacted records were recovered, and subsequent December month-end Bulk Data verification found no issues.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected Bulk Invoice data for shipments in FDPs including Okayama, Iwate, and Shikoku that were not included in closing data sent to KB.', 'After data extraction, an update SQL set the sent-to-KB flag based on the order number rather than the shipment.', 'When one shipment under an order was selected for KB processing, the SQL updated the flag for all shipments of that order.', 'Missing November 30 records had X_IF_STATUS set to Y before the SQL fix, causing them to be excluded from Bulk Invoice processing.', 'Recovery Bulk Invoice data was created and manually sent to KB for identified impacted records.', 'December month-end Bulk Data was verified and no further issue was found.']
Root Cause: The post-extraction update SQL updated the sent-to-KB flag, X_IF_STATUS, using the order number instead of the shipment, incorrectly marking all shipments for an order as sent to KB.
Resolution: The SQL was corrected in all production environments to update flags by shipment, recovery Bulk Invoice data was generated and sent to KB for impacted records, and month-end Bulk Invoice executions were monitored through December.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: An error occurred when Liability Insurance Information entered by the user did not match a Liability Insurance record in the master. The existing behavior could not resolve the insurance name and displayed an error instead of handling the unmatched master data as a zero-cost item. The fix was implemented in UAT-1 and released to Prod to create a zero-price Liability Insurance Quote Line Item when no matching master record exists.
Important Findings: ["The entered liability insurance information was not maintained in the master for the applicable combination of MD Classification 'M', Insurance Vehicle Type 'Omnibus', and Mainland Category 'Mainland'.", 'Liability Insurance Term values 1 through 13 were identified as available for the applicable master-data combination.', 'The initial error message occurred because the system could not find the insurance name, rather than because no insurance information had been entered.', 'The required behavior was to retain the expense name and display a zero amount when master data does not match, consistent with Taxes and other expenses behavior.', 'The implemented fix creates a Liability Insurance record in the Quote Line Item with zero price when Liability Insurance is not maintained in the master.', 'The change was completed on UAT-1 and subsequently released to Prod.']
Root Cause: No Liability Insurance master record matched the user-entered Liability Insurance Information, and the existing logic treated the unresolved insurance name as an error instead of creating a zero-price item.
Resolution: Modified the logic to create a dummy Liability Insurance in the Quote Line Item with zero price when no matching Liability Insurance master record is found; the change was tested on UAT-1 and released to Prod.

Investigation Summary: The Order Detail BIP report failed to generate for Trailer and Forklift sales orders. A fix was deployed to UAT1, approved for production, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['The affected function was generation of the Order Detail BIP report.', 'Tax rate is calculated in the Sales Quote based on the Planned Delivery Date and is passed to the Sales Order.', 'Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes did not validate Planned Delivery Date before approval.', 'When Planned Delivery Date was empty, Tax rate remained null in both the Sales Quote and Sales Order.', 'The null Tax rate caused the BIP report generation failure.', 'The affected sales order was recovered, allowing BIP to be printed.']
Root Cause: Trailer and Forklift Sales Quotes lacked Planned Delivery Date validation, allowing approval with an empty date. This prevented Tax rate calculation and passed a null Tax rate to the Sales Order, causing the Order Detail BIP report to fail.
Resolution: A fix addressing the issue was deployed to UAT1 and then released to Prod after approval; the affected sales order was recovered so BIP could be printed.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: NV Quote and NV Sales Order contained different model codes because users could directly edit fields in the Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items. Affected records were recovered, and the editability issue was corrected and validated in FDP-UAT1 before release to PROD. The fix was released to PROD on 13 November.
Important Findings: ['The Chassis & Options tab in NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories.', 'Users changed the model code directly in NV Sales Order instead of changing it in NV Quote and synchronizing the Quote to the Sales Order.', 'The correct business process is to update the model code in NV Quote and then sync the Quote to NV Sales Order.', 'The before-fix condition was available in FDP-RT2, where SO# A000055765 had editable Chassis & Options line-item fields.', 'In FDP-UAT1, fields in NV Sales Order were made read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#.', 'Recovery was completed for the shared affected records; no additional affected records were found in other FDP environments.']
Root Cause: The Chassis & Options tab of NV Sales Order line items was editable for some responsibility categories, allowing users to directly modify model codes in NV Sales Order and create mismatches with NV Quote.
Resolution: Made NV Sales Order Chassis & Options fields read-only, including Product Name, Line#, and C#, validated the change in FDP-UAT1, and released the fix to PROD on 13 November.
Technical Entities: ['NV Quote', 'NV Sales Order', 'NVSO', 'Chassis & Options tab', 'Product Name', 'Line#', 'C#', 'model code', 'FDP-Shikoku', 'FDP-UAT1', 'FDP-RT2', 'PROD', 'Production', 'SO# A000055765', 'A000080119', 'A000088119', 'Recovery_Records_FDP.xlsx', 'Cubastion']

Root Cause: Incorrect master data: the Lubrication Master file executed for UAT1 and FDP-Okayama contained Generic Flag = 'N' for dummy lubrication parts, causing 'Outsourcing Lubricant Carry-in' to default to 'N'.
Resolution: Recovery was completed by resetting the Generic Flag to 'Y' for the dummy lubrication parts. The SOP will be updated to validate the Generic Flag for dummy parts whenever a Lubrication Master file is received.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Power BI export failed for JPN when two columns had identical Japanese translations, producing duplicate alias names in the export query. English exports succeeded because Power BI automatically appended suffixes such as _1 and _2. A fix to make the Japanese field titles unique was deployed to UAT and then released to production.
Important Findings: ['Two columns with the same Japanese translation generated the same alias name in the Power BI export query.', 'Duplicate column names made the export query invalid and caused the error: “File creation failure – An error occurred while executing the query for the data export operation.”', 'English Power BI exports handled duplicate aliases by appending suffixes such as _1 and _2.', 'For JPN, adding _2 to one duplicated field title prevented title duplication.', 'The fix was deployed to UAT and subsequently released to production.']
Root Cause: Duplicate Japanese translations caused two exported columns to receive the same alias name, resulting in an invalid Power BI export query with duplicate column names.
Resolution: Updated one of the duplicate Japanese field titles by adding _2, then deployed the fix to UAT and production.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: In UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW", using Change Records to update Manual Discount% after selecting all quote line items with Ctrl+A changed the editable field initially clicked by the user. The behavior was reproduced in Service Quotes and parts quote and was identified as a Siebel Vanilla functionality defect rather than a business-process configuration issue. Users were instructed to initiate the operation from a read-only field or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred when a user clicked an editable field, selected all lines with Ctrl+A, and used Change Records to update Manual Discount%.', 'After confirming Change Records, the editable field initially selected in step 1 was changed.', 'The behavior was reproduced on Service Quotes and parts quote, including UAT1 test record "1-6WGYRW".', 'The current business process configuration was confirmed to be correct.', 'Change Records is a Siebel Vanilla functionality, and the behavior was identified as a Siebel bug.', 'As a workaround, users should click a read-only field before using Ctrl+A and Change Records, or manually select records if the cursor is in an editable field.']
Root Cause: A Siebel bug in the vanilla Change Records functionality causes the initially selected editable field to be changed when all records are selected with Ctrl+A and a bulk update is performed.
Resolution: Communicate the operational workaround to Hakodate branch users: start the Change Records operation from a read-only field, or manually select records when the cursor is in an editable field.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Duplicate JVs were created for D2S Invoice records with a blank PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) because the processing flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation. The flag-update logic was corrected and tested in UAT8 so PO-blank records are processed only once. The fix was deployed to Production in the 23rd October FDP release, and recovery data was completed for the affected duplicate JV records.
Important Findings: ['JV creation is triggered when the D2S Invoice flag is not "S".', 'The existing flag-update logic required PO Num, Invoice Num, and Inv Dt to be non-null.', 'PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) being blank is normal for D2S invoices received by Siebel.', 'For PO-blank records, the flag was not updated to "S" after JV creation, allowing duplicate JVs to be created.', 'The issue affected three records on Chugoku.', 'Recovery was required for duplicate JV types D2S Inv Amt, D2S Inv CommFee, and D2S Inv CT.']
Root Cause: The flag-update filter required PO Num to be non-null. When PO Number (X_ATTRIB_02) was blank, the D2S Invoice record was not updated to flag "S" after JV creation and was eligible for duplicate JV creation.
Resolution: Updated the flag-update logic so records with blank PO Num are updated to "S" after processing, tested the change in UAT8, and deployed it to Production in the 23rd October FDP release. Created and completed Production recovery data for the duplicate JVs.

Root Cause: A concurrent update to the same Sales Order line-item record during Quote-to-Sales Order synchronization caused a Siebel record-update conflict, preventing the Sales Order from synchronizing to the latest Quote revision.
Resolution: The affected record was recovered on Wakayama Prod. The proposed preventive measure was to instruct users not to update the same record simultaneously from different sessions or screens.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Status Code values differed between SC and FDP because each environment sourced the value from a different table and represented a different status type. Changes were implemented and validated in FDP UAT, with the final Status Code LOV filter update deployed to production for Report #1-15A across all FDPs. Validation in PBI-PROD confirmed the change was correct and the incident was resolved.
Important Findings: ['In FDP, Status Code is sourced from WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F and represents Order Status.', 'In SC, Status Code is sourced from W_SRVREQ_MD and represents Service Request Status.', 'The differing source tables caused different Status Code filter values between SC and FDP.', 'The Order Code LOV displayed correctly in FORCE FDP (UAT), but the line item Order Code (JC Status) was initially not displayed.', 'The requested LOV change for Report #1-05 was withdrawn because it was technically difficult.', 'The Status Code LOV for Report #1-15A was changed correctly for all FDPs in PBI-PROD.']
Root Cause: SC and FDP used different source tables for Status Code: WC_SERVICE_ORDER_F in FDP for Order Status and W_SRVREQ_MD in SC for Service Request Status.
Resolution: Deployed the Status Code LOV filter change for Report #1-15A to production for all FDPs; the change was validated successfully in PBI-PROD.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Invoice data for Parts Purchase Order line items was not inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch when the D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file. The insertion logic was corrected on FDP-UAT1, including a filter-condition update for null X_ATTRIB_02 values, and was released to Production on 23rd October. Historical mismatch records were recovered across affected FDPs and their creation dates were aligned to the invoice-received date.
Important Findings: ['D2S Invoice Mismatch excluded invoice data when D2S SO Item Number and Product values in a PO line item did not match the D2S invoice file.', 'A filter condition failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null, causing incorrect values to be selected for records with blank PO numbers.', 'After the fix, invoice data was inserted into D2S Invoice Mismatch even when PO line items differed from the D2S Invoice file.', 'D2S Invoice Mismatch records are stored in CX_MISM_TOB / siebel.CX_MISM_TOB.', 'Recovery was required for mismatch records on Iwate, Aomori, Shikoku, and FDP Chugoku; recovered records had their creation dates updated to the invoice-received date.', 'Creation dates for invoice 8000115382 items 000010 and 000020 in siebel.CX_MISM_TOB were corrected to August 4, 2025 to match siebel.cx_d2s_recon.']
Root Cause: D2S Invoice Mismatch insertion logic excluded invoice data when PO line-item D2S SO Item Number and Product did not match the D2S invoice file; a related filter condition also failed when X_ATTRIB_02 was null.
Resolution: Updated the insertion and filter conditions on FDP-UAT1, released the fix to Production in the 23rd October scheduled FDP release, and recovered affected mismatch records with corrected creation dates.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Copied Job Cards could receive an incorrect Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id, resulting in a Chassis# different from the source Job Card. The issue occurred when duplicate vehicle registration-field values caused the copied Job Card to be reassigned to a different vehicle. The fix was validated in FDP UAT-1 and released to all FDP-PROD environments on 25 September.
Important Findings: ['Copy Job Card initially populates Asset Id, MF Asset Id, and MF Vehicle Id from the parent Job Card.', 'After Registration Number (L/#) is copied, Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id are updated from Auto Vehicle using Registration No Class No, Registration No. Land Name Area Name, Registration No Japanese Kana, and Registration No Sequence No.', 'Two vehicles in Chugoku prod had identical registration-field values, causing copied JC I050382306 to use chassis# FB51AB-552056 instead of chassis# FS54VZ-532935.', 'The fix was verified in FDP UAT-1 using copied JC I001298557 and source JC I001273076; the copied Job Card received the correct Chassis# (Key#) from the VM- tab.', 'The patch was released in the 25 September scheduled FDP release and applied to all FDP-PROD environments.']
Root Cause: Duplicate vehicle values for the registration fields used by Auto Vehicle caused a copied Job Card to update its Asset Id and MF Vehicle Id to a different vehicle, resulting in an incorrect Chassis#.
Resolution: The issue was fixed, validated in FDP UAT-1, and the patch was deployed to all FDP-PROD environments in the 25 September scheduled FDP release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident matched MFTBCFFR-4243 and involved a Trade-In Assessment that could not be deleted after the Trade-In Flag was manually changed from "Y" to "N" in NV Quote Header revision 2. Unchecking the flag makes related Trade-In fields read-only, preventing required backend updates during assessment deletion. The issue is resolved by rechecking the Trade-In Flag to "Y" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment.
Important Findings: ['In revision 1, the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header was set to "Y".', 'In revision 2, the user manually unchecked the Trade-In Flag, changing it to "N".', 'When the Trade-In Flag is unchecked, related Trade-In fields become read-only.', 'Read-only Trade-In fields prevent backend field updates required to delete the Trade-In Assessment.', 'The correct process is to delete the Trade-In Assessment first, then uncheck the Trade-In Flag.']
Root Cause: The Trade-In Flag was changed to "N" before deleting the Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates required for deletion.
Resolution: Recheck the Trade-In Flag in NV Quote Header to "Y", delete the Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Button enablement in FDP used an RF status condition even though RF Status is not available in FDP, causing incorrect button behavior. The implementation was revised to control Send Recycle Fee, Modify/Change Order, and CUT/Cancel Order behavior using TOB and Recycle Fee Order statuses, including a one-day rule based on receipt of a successful TOB response. The final changes were tested in UAT1, approved for production, and released in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.
Important Findings: ['The original button logic depended on RF STATUS = Null, but RF Status is not used in FDP.', 'The requested behavior was to make the Request for modification and CUT buttons unavailable from the day after a successful TOB response when the recycle order status is Completed or Recycle Order Changed.', 'The One Day Window requirement was corrected: CUT and Modify buttons must be enabled for the full day on which a successful TOB response is received, not the day the TOB request is sent.', 'For UAT1 verification, a TOB response was simulated for Chassis Order # B001217339 and Recycle Fee Order # B001217574; the record Last Modified date was used to identify the successful-response date.', 'The implementation also needed to preserve Send Recycle Fee availability after CUT success or a modification TOB error, rather than relying only on TOB response date and TOB status.', 'The incident was released to Production in the 23 October 2025 scheduled FDP release.']
Root Cause: Legacy RF STATUS-based button-enable conditions were retained although RF Status is not available in FDP, resulting in incorrect enablement control for the TOB-related buttons.
Resolution: Reworked the FDP button-control logic to use TOB Status and Recycle Fee Order Status, with CUT and Modify enabled only on the date a successful TOB response is received; the finalized changes were released to Production on 23 October 2025.

Investigation Summary: A record was reported as visible in Siebel but missing from PBI Reports; sample order Q050163081 was provided.
