Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Zero-amount Journal Vouchers (JVs) were created because JV-creation filters did not consistently evaluate the same Base Amount fields used by the JV. In Okinawa prod, the fix from MFTBCFFR-3779 was ineffective for two Journal Event types because of an extra space in the deployed filter. The Okinawa fix was released on July 24, 2025, and the corrected filters for the remaining Journal Event types were validated in UAT/UAT1 and released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.
Important Findings: ['Zero-amount JVs were found in FDP prod for multiple Journal Event types where the filter field differed from the JV Base Amount field.', 'The JV-creation filter is intended to prevent JV creation when Base Amount equals zero.', 'For Okinawa prod, the MFTBCFFR-3779 fix for "Service Correction Sales Amount Non-Taxable" and "Service Correction Sales Amount Red Slip Non-Taxable" failed because of an extra space in the deployed filter.', 'The corrective logic uses the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount" and applies a "Base amount not equal to zero" condition.', 'The fix was validated in UAT1, where zero-amount JVs were no longer created.']
Root Cause: Incorrect JV-creation filter configuration: filters used fields different from the JV Base Amount fields; additionally, an extra space in the deployed filter prevented the prior MFTBCFFR-3779 fix from working in Okinawa prod.
Resolution: Released a corrected "Base amount not equal to zero" filter using the same fields as "Credit Base Amount" and "Debit Base Amount". The Okinawa prod correction was released on July 24, 2025, and changes for the remaining Journal Event types were released to FDP Production on August 27, 2025.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned Entity Transfer behavior for Sales Rep transfers, particularly transfers within special sales. Multiple UAT issues were identified, including unavailable target users due to organization and position configuration, duplicate Position Id values, and incorrect user filtering. The final implementation restricts Sales Rep Transfer to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position, and was deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Entity Transfer initially displayed only configured position types; requested additional position types were added to the Entity Transfer logic on UAT1.', 'A transfer between D0X20852 and D0X20851 was blocked because their primary organizations differed: D0X20852 was in Default Organization, 000000000O, while D0X20851 was in Okayama East Branch, 10.', 'A transfer did not reflect because both users had the same Position Id; the Position Id issue was corrected.', "Person selection was unavailable for one Sales Order because no user was assigned to the current Sales Rep's position; the position was assigned to users.", "The final Entity Transfer rule allows Sales Rep Transfer only to users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position.", 'The self-approval validation was separately identified as introduced to FDP through CR-0836 and was removed from NV Quote on UAT1 for testing.']
Root Cause: Entity Transfer user-selection and transfer behavior did not meet the required special-sales transfer criteria; additional issues were caused by different user organizations, duplicate Position Id values, and missing user assignments for the current Sales Rep position.
Resolution: Updated Entity Transfer to allow Sales Rep Transfer only among users in the same Organization and with the same Position type as the Primary Sales Rep's Position; corrected duplicate Position Id configuration and assigned missing positions to users. The changes were deployed to Production in the 25 September FDP release.

Investigation Summary: Bulk invoice data was not sent on 30 June because the existing logic determines the send schedule from the closing date of the original account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order. Important Findings: ['Recovery was completed and the data was linked to KB again.', 'Bulk invoice data is fetched using "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, which represents the original Account.', 'The closing date used for bulk invoice processing is taken from the account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code".', 'The original Account closing date was 20; therefore, data was expected to be sent on 20 July, not 30 June.', 'Current logic does not fetch bulk invoice data using the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code".', 'A logic change is being tracked under project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.']
Root Cause: The bulk invoice workflow uses the closing date of the original Account identified by "Ship to Basic Account Code" in Change Order, rather than the closing date of "Bill to basic Account Code". Because that account's closing date was 20, the data was not scheduled to send on 30 June.
Resolution: Recovered the incident data by linking it to KB again. The required logic change is being handled through project CR MFTBCFFR-4402.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Duplicate Journal Vouchers were created for Body Building Orders in FDP Production, including Chugoku prod. Investigation found that the validation introduced under MFTBCFFR-3809 checked only for an existing Completed JV trigger, allowing a second trigger while the original trigger was still in progress. The validation was updated and tested in UAT1, then released to FDP Production on 27th August.
Important Findings: ['Affected duplicate Journal Vouchers were recovered using reverse Journal Vouchers and linked to KB through the daily batch.', 'The MFTBCFFR-3809 validation prevented new JV triggers only when a Completed trigger existed for the Body Building Order.', 'A duplicate Journal Voucher was created two minutes after the original because the original JV trigger had not yet reached Completed status.', 'The corrected validation prevents creation of another JV trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of status.', 'UAT testing confirmed that multiple Shipment Details responses from IBOS send the Journal Voucher trigger only once.', 'The fix was deployed to FDP Production in the 27th August planned release.']
Root Cause: The validation check added by MFTBCFFR-3809 searched only for existing Completed JV triggers. When another trigger was received before the original trigger completed, the validation did not detect the in-progress trigger and created a duplicate Journal Voucher.
Resolution: Updated the JV-trigger validation to block creation of a new trigger when any trigger exists for the original Journal Voucher, regardless of trigger status. The fix was implemented in UAT1 and released to FDP Production on 27th August.

Root Cause: The user unchecked the UV Trade-In Flag before deleting the UV Trade-In Assessment, causing related Trade-In fields to become read-only and blocking the backend updates needed for deletion.
Resolution: Recheck the UV Trade-In Flag to "Y", delete the UV Trade-In Assessment, and only then uncheck the flag if required.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Users could add an Option line item through the Parts and Internal Work Applet in a UV quote by entering it in Part#. Options were not displayed in the Parts and Internal Work screen, preventing users from deleting them; saving produced an error while adding the record. A validation restricting permitted product types was implemented in the FDP UAT Environment and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.
Important Findings: ['The Parts and Internal Work Applet allowed an Option to be entered in Part# and saved as a line item.', 'The Parts and Internal Work screen displayed only Parts, so Option line items were not visible and could not be deleted by users.', 'Saving the affected record displayed an error but still added the record; a UAT1 reference was 1-19MOBS.', 'Production recovery was completed before the permanent fix was deployed.', 'The fix restricts the Parts and Internal Work Applet to Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant product types.']
Root Cause: The Parts and Internal Work Applet lacked validation to prevent unsupported product types, allowing Option line items to be added even though the related screen displayed only Parts.
Resolution: Implemented validation in the Parts and Internal Work Applet to allow only Parts, Labor, Accessories, and Lubricant. The fix was deployed to the FDP UAT Environment on 27 June 2025 and released to Prod on 10 July 2025.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: PO allocation failures occurred in FDP Shikoku, Okayama, Aomori, and Chugoku for Parts Purchase Orders received from D2S; the issue was also observed in the SC version. Investigation determined that D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger for parts that had not been registered in order line items. Affected orders were recovered in the relevant production environments, and preventing recurrence requires order-line-item registration before cancellation.
Important Findings: ['Current logic registers parts in order line items only when the received part is Norm(ZFTN) or Bans(ZFTS).', 'D2S sent ZFTX triggers directly to cancel parts that were not present in the order line items.', 'Cancellation and PO allocation failed because the target parts did not exist in the order line items.', 'The issue affected FDP and was also observed in the SC version.', 'Affected orders were recovered in FDP - PROD, FDPC - PROD, FDPA - PROD, and FDPO - PROD.']
Root Cause: D2S sent a ZFTX cancellation trigger before the relevant part had been registered in the order line items. Since only Norm(ZFTN) and Bans(ZFTS) parts are registered under the current logic, the cancelled parts did not exist in the line items and could not be cancelled or allocated.
Resolution: Recovered the affected orders in the applicable FDP production environments. To prevent recurrence, order line item registration must occur before the ZFTX cancellation trigger is processed.

Investigation Summary: IBOS estimate responses were not reflected because new body specification/bodywork records in the IBOS response were not created. The backend data map operation was configured as "update", which only modified existing records. The operation was changed to "upsert" in UAT so that existing records are updated and new records can be created; IBOS response testing and demonstration remained pending.
Important Findings: ['The issue affected reflection of IBOS estimate responses for NV Body quotes.', 'The existing backend data map operation was set to "update", preventing creation of new body specification/bodywork records received from IBOS.', 'The configuration issue was associated with changes made when the Body Building sub-quote was removed from FDP.', 'Changing the data map operation to "upsert" allows both updates to existing records and creation of new records from the IBOS response.', 'The fix was reported as implemented and tested on UAT/UAT1, but end-to-end IBOS response testing was still pending.', 'Requested verification was to submit an NV quote with a body using "Submit to IBOS" and confirm that the IBOS quote response updates the relevant records.']
Root Cause: The backend data map operation was set to "update", which only updated existing records and prevented creation of new body specification/bodywork records included in IBOS estimate responses.
Resolution: Changed the backend data map operation from "update" to "upsert" in UAT/UAT1, enabling IBOS responses to update existing records and create new body specification/bodywork records as needed.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Stock records were visible in SIEBEL/Siebel DB but missing from the PBI 5-02 report because they were excluded by ODI filtering conditions. The affected Shikoku parts were corrected by changing their item category to LUMF and creating/executing the required Price Master; recovery completed and the records became visible in PBI 5-02. For part #101244115, the remaining root cause was identified as an inventory update timestamp outside the effective date range of its price-list item.
Important Findings: ['Shikoku Branch 42 parts HB06MS2, HB511, HD72T, HD72U, HD72V, and MB05A were present in SIEBEL but absent from PBI 5-02.', "These parts were excluded from the PBI datamart by ODI because they failed the condition S_PRI_LST.SUBTYPE_CD = 'Parts Price List'.", 'The affected parts were incorrectly categorized as NORM instead of LUMF, so the expected LUMF price lists with List price and D/N price set to 0 had not been created.', 'After the item category was manually changed to LUMF, Price Master was created and executed, and the affected parts appeared in PBI 5-02.', "Part #101244115 failed the ODI condition S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD BETWEEN S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_START_DT AND NVL(S_PRI_LST_ITEM.EFF_END_DT,'31-12-9999') because its LAST_UPD timestamps were later than the configured EFF_END_DT of 2025-04-26."]
Root Cause: Invalid or missing price-list master data caused ODI exclusions: the affected parts were categorized as NORM rather than LUMF and lacked a 'Parts Price List'; for part #101244115, S_PROD_INV.LAST_UPD was outside the S_PRI_LST_ITEM effective-date range.
Resolution: Manually changed the affected parts' item category to LUMF, created and executed the Price Master, and completed recovery so the parts became visible in the PBI 5-02 report.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Journal Voucher data for Liability Insurance Orders was not sent to KB because the department code was null. Investigation found that migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), which resulted in missing department code in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher. The impacted orders were patched, recovery JVs were created, and recovery data was added to Prod for transmission to KB in the nightly batch.
Important Findings: ['On 22 May, a Journal Voucher was created after spreadsheet approval but was not sent to KB because its department code was not set.', 'Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id).', 'A null Primary Position Id caused the department code to be null in both the Insurance Order and the Liability Insurance Journal Voucher.', 'Liability Insurance Orders with status "Spreadsheet Approved" were excluded from the recovery.', "PR_POSTN_ID was patched by mapping the Sales Rep's Primary Position for the impacted Insurance orders.", 'Recovery JVs were created and added to Prod for delivery to KB in the nightly batch.']
Root Cause: Migrated Liability Insurance Orders had a null PR_POSTN_ID (Primary Position Id), causing the department code to be null in the Insurance Order and Journal Voucher and preventing JV data from being sent to KB.
Resolution: Patched PR_POSTN_ID for impacted Liability Insurance Orders using the Sales Rep's Primary Position, created recovery JVs, and added the recovery data to Prod for transmission to KB.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A blank trade-in line item could be created in an NV Quote when the AR# was removed and the line item was saved during a quote revision. Replication in UAT confirmed that clearing the AR# cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id, resulting in the blank line item. A validation was implemented and tested in UAT to prevent saving a trade-in line item with a blank assessment number, then released to PROD on June 26, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was replicated in UAT using NV Quote #: 1-KHY8Z, Rev-3.', "In NV Quote #: 1-IQZEL, Rev-2, removing AR#: H000001601 from a trade-in vehicle while creating Rev-3 and then deleting the record cleared the trade-in line item's asset_id.", 'A new trade-in vehicle with AR#: H000001602 could then be added while the cleared asset_id caused a blank line item to display in the NV Quote.', 'The implemented validation prevents users from saving a trade-in line item when the AR# / assessment number is blank.', 'Users can still update the AR# through the standard process or delete the trade-in line item.', 'The UAT test record was UAT1, NV Quote #: 1-6AFG8S; the validation error message was changed to “Assessment No. is a required field and cannot be left blank.”']
Root Cause: The trade-in line item process allowed the AR# to be removed and the line item saved, which cleared asset_id and created a blank trade-in line item in the NV Quote.
Resolution: Implemented validation in UAT and released it to PROD on June 26, 2025, preventing a trade-in line item from being saved with a blank AR# / assessment number.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Statistics were not collected for tables in the Wakayama environment because the Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked tables below its configured data-volume cutoff. The affected tables were unlocked and statistics were gathered, resolving the incident on 19 May 2025 at 13:45 JST. As a permanent measure, Wakayama will use monthly manual statistics collection through DBMS statistics instead of coe_Siebel_stats.sql.
Important Findings: ['coe_Siebel_stats.sql locks tables with fewer rows, preventing statistics collection for those tables.', 'The Wakayama tables had insufficient data volume to exceed the script cutoff value.', 'The cutoff value is defined by the Oracle-provided and recommended script and cannot be changed by the support team.', 'A similar issue occurred in the FDP Hakodate environment in February 2025.', 'Unlocking statistics on the affected tables followed by gathering statistics restored collection.']
Root Cause: The Oracle-recommended coe_Siebel_stats.sql script locked Wakayama tables whose data volume was below its configured cutoff, preventing statistics from being collected.
Resolution: Unlocked statistics for the affected tables and reran statistics gathering. Wakayama will manually collect statistics monthly using DBMS statistics rather than coe_Siebel_stats.sql.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The March 31 Bulk Invoice file from Cubastion showed that all referenced JCs were successfully sent from Siebel to KB, so the Bulk Invoice process was operating normally. The investigation identified that the Account master linkage from Siebel to KB had been intentionally suspended for all accounts in Shikoku Production pending deployment of the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR. KB was performing manual recovery while the interface remained suspended, and the incident was closed as not being a system issue.
Important Findings: ['All referenced JCs were included in the March EOM (March 31) Bulk Invoice file and were successfully sent to KB.', 'Siebel sends Bulk Invoice data to KB; no information was available regarding CSS Invoice processing.', 'MFTBCFFR-3040 addressed incorrect mapping in some Account master data columns sent to KB; the incident fix was deployed to all FDP environments.', 'A further CR requested after MFTBCFFR-3040 remained pending for Production deployment.', 'Under MFTBCFFR-3149, the complete Account master interface was stopped in Shikoku Production for all accounts, not only specific account codes.', 'Account code 1000007404, created in April, was not sent to KB because Account master bulk processing had been stopped before April.']
Root Cause: The complete Account master linkage from Siebel to KB was intentionally suspended in Shikoku Production at Miyauchi's request until the MFTBCFFR-3040 CR is deployed to Production.
Resolution: KB performed manual recovery while the Account master linkage remained suspended pending CR development and Production deployment; the incident was closed as not being a system issue.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned activity status changes in the UI and the relationship between Activity status and Job Card (JC) status. Investigation confirmed that users could manually perform all standard Activity status transitions. A fix was implemented so that closing a JC automatically sets the Activity status to "Work Completed" and makes it read-only; it was validated in UAT 1 and released to production on 26 May 2025.
Important Findings: ['The standard Activity status flow is "Open" → "Request for Reservation" → "Reservation Confirmed" → "Work Completed" → "Closed".', 'Users were able to manually change Activity status through the UI, including all standard transitions.', 'When Job Card (JC) status is set to "Closed", the fix updates the Activity status to "Work Completed" regardless of its prior status.', 'After an Activity status is updated to "Work Completed", the status becomes read-only and cannot be manually modified.', 'The fix was implemented and validated in UAT 1 before release to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.']
Root Cause: The UI allowed users to manually modify Activity status, and Activity status was not automatically set to "Work Completed" when the associated Job Card (JC) status was set to "Closed".
Resolution: Implemented automatic Activity status update to "Work Completed" when JC status is set to "Closed", regardless of previous Activity status, and made the Activity status read-only after that update. The fix was validated in UAT 1 and released to the FDP production environment on 26 May 2025.

Investigation Summary: A Consumption Tax JV line was missing for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event because a search specification evaluated a consumption tax amount of 0.8 as zero. The search specification was corrected to use the proper rounding behavior, validated in UAT-1/UAT-01, and released to Production on 14 May.
Important Findings: ['JV line creation uses a Search Specification to prevent creation of zero-amount JV lines.', 'The consumption tax amount of 0.8 should have been rounded to 1.', 'Incorrect rounding in the Search Specification treated 0.8 as 0.', 'As a result, no JV line was created for the "Job Card Sales CT" journal event.', 'The affected JC was recovered and the Consumption Tax JV was added in Production.', 'The corrected Search Specification was tested in UAT-1/UAT-01 and released to Production on 14 May.']
Root Cause: The Search Specification used to determine whether a tax amount was zero applied incorrect rounding, causing consumption tax amount 0.8 to be treated as 0 and suppressing creation of the "Job Card Sales CT" JV line.
Resolution: Corrected the Search Specification rounding behavior, validated the fix in UAT-1/UAT-01, released it to Production on 14 May, and recovered the affected JC by adding the Consumption Tax JV in Production.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Incorrect Total PO Cost on the Service Purchase Order (SPO) was investigated in UAT1 for SPO J001294885 and JC I001294884. The behavior was caused by the configured labor-line quantity calculation logic for labor code .004330, not a system defect. Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N corrected the SPO value, and the incident was withdrawn.
Important Findings: ['For labor code .004330, Quantity Requested defaults to 1 when Zero Effort Flag is Y, Billing Type is not Customer, and PO Cost Flag is N.', 'The Quantity Requested default of 1 is applied regardless of actual labor effort or operation time.', 'The resulting Total PO Cost can be higher than the actual cost because it is calculated using the default quantity of 1.', 'The behavior is designed according to the existing validation rules.', 'Changing the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N caused the correct value to be reflected in the SPO in UAT1.']
Root Cause: Labor code .004330 was configured with Zero Effort Flag = Y, Billing Type other than Customer, and PO Cost Flag = N, which triggered designed logic that defaulted Quantity Requested to 1 and produced an incorrect Total PO Cost.
Resolution: Changed the Zero Effort Flag from Y to N in UAT1, which corrected the value in the SPO. The incident was withdrawn as a flag-setting issue rather than a system issue.

Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected orders. Remaining orders will generate JVs automatically after their status is updated to "Shipment Instructed".

Root Cause: The "Create Spreadsheet" button could be enabled through the "Liability Clerical Error" workflow while "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date" was not valid, allowing commission calculation to run with incomplete order data.
Resolution: Updated the "Create Spreadsheet" enablement condition to require a valid "Vehicle Liability Insurance Certificate Issue Date". Important Findings: ['"51: Complaint" job cards cannot be directly linked to a new car order by design.', 'New vehicle order A000121450 was linked by creating a "22: New car modification (movement)" job card, setting the new car order in the internal order field, and changing the JC Type to "51: Claim" before completion.', 'The system allowed the linkage because internal-order values persisted after the JC Type was changed.', 'The fix resets "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type is changed.', 'UAT-1 validation confirmed that changing JC Type from "22" to another type, including "26", correctly resets the values.', 'The fix was released to Production in the 13 September scheduled FDP release.']
Root Cause: Service Job Card did not reset the internal-order fields when the JC Type was changed, allowing a new car order linked under JC Type "22: New car modification (movement)" to remain linked after changing the job card to "51: Claim".
Resolution: Implemented a Service Job Card change to reset "Internal Order (Charge To)" and "Internal Order Number" whenever the JC Type changes; validated in FDP UAT1/UAT-1 and deployed to Production on 13 September.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Sales approval was blocked because no Recycle Fee order was mapped to the Sales Order for C# 10360. Investigation confirmed that TOB did not send the D21F file, so no Recycle Fee order was created; only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received. Recovery was completed and Sales Posting was completed without a recycling order. The reported “major component is missing” message was considered inappropriate for this rare scenario and will be monitored for recurrence.
Important Findings: ['No D21F file was received for C# 10360.', 'Only D21A, D21R, and D21N files were received for C# 10360.', 'Without a D21F file, no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.', 'During Generate Approval/Request Approval, Siebel validates whether a Recycle Fee order is mapped to the Sales Order; this behavior is the same as SC.', 'The “major component is missing” error message was reported as incorrect when the Recycle Fee order does not exist.', 'The case was considered rare; corrective measures will be considered if similar incidents recur.']
Root Cause: TOB did not provide the D21F file for C# 10360, so no Recycle Fee order was created or mapped to the Sales Order.
Resolution: Recovery was completed, allowing delivery approval and Sales Posting to complete without a recycling order. The incident was closed with monitoring for recurrence.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A Payer Change Order retained the previous Closed Date after the user changed the Bill to Basic Account, causing bulk invoice data to be excluded from the expected closing-date processing and sent to KB at EOM instead. The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1, where Closed Date and Payment Term now update based on the newly selected payer. The fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to PROD on 12 June 2025.
Important Findings: ['For Account 0000205096, Change Order K000065493 retained an EOM closing date although the account closing date was 25.', 'In a Payer Change Order, Bill to Basic Account and Ship to Basic Account are initially retrieved from JCO.', 'Changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account did not refresh Closed Date or Payment Term; the prior values remained on the change order.', 'Because Closed Date remained EOM rather than 25, the change order was not sent to KB with the expected bulk invoice data; JC lines and change order lines were sent on 31 March.', 'The corrected behavior was verified in UAT-1 for Payer Change and Payer and Price Change scenarios.']
Root Cause: When the payer was changed in Bill to Basic Account on a Payer Change Order, the system did not update Closed Date and Payment Term from the newly selected payer, leaving the previous EOM Closed Date on the change order.
Resolution: Updated FDP so that changing the payer in Bill to Basic Account on a Service Change Order refreshes Closed Date and Payment Term according to the new payer. The fix was deployed to FDP UAT-1, validated, and released to PROD on 12 June 2025; recovery bulk invoice data was also shared with MDIS after approval.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident involved incorrect Credit and Debit Department Code assignment in PO GR JV for Trade-In purchase orders. The existing logic used the NV Sales Order Last Approver, but the required logic for NV Trade-In is to derive the Branch Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep. The fix was validated in UAT1, affected JVs were recovered, and the change was released to Production on April 24.
Important Findings: ['The original PO GR JV logic assigned Credit and Debit Department Code based on the NV Sales Order Last Approver/PO creator.', 'For NV Trade-In, both Credit and Debit Department Code must be set from the Branch Code of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep.', 'The fix was implemented in UAT1 and UAT passed with AR#H000046387 and PO# F001294580.', 'Alternate approver D0X20883 received the NV Sales Order approval request for Sales Rep D0X20897; approving the order created the Trade-In PO with D0X20883 as creator.', 'UV Trade-In does not require this fix because the department code on the JV Trade-In line is derived from the Assessment request, not the UV Sales Order final approval.', 'Affected JVs were recovered before the Production release.']
Root Cause: The NV Trade-In PO GR JV department-code logic incorrectly derived Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Last Approver instead of the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code.
Resolution: Updated the NV Trade-In PO GR JV logic to set Credit and Debit Department Code from the NV Sales Order Sales Rep Branch Code, validated the change in UAT1, recovered affected JVs, and released the fix to Production on April 24.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Incomplete address data on the account used by the NV Quote/Sales Order caused an approval-processing error while downstream processing still marked approval as completed and generated duplicate Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and JVs. The affected account address is the account selected in the Contractor Name field, whose address is sent to Falcon. Duplicate JVs and Falcon records were recovered, and validation was implemented in NV Quote to prevent approval generation when the selected contractor account has incomplete address data. The validated fix was released to PROD on April 14.
Important Findings: ['The original failure was reproduced on UAT 6 with Sales Order A000026083 and customer code 0000032930.', 'During the second Sales Posting approval from Inbox, an error prevented Inbox approval, but approval history showed Approved, the order moved to Sales Posting Completed, and a Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Order was created.', 'Rejecting the Inbox approval and regenerating approvals could create multiple Planned Pool Cost - Shipment Orders and duplicate JVs.', 'The account address data used by the Sales Order was incomplete; missing city code/address fields, including Oaza/Common Name for account 0000029653, triggered the issue.', "Validation checks only the address of the account selected in the Contractor Name field because Falcon sends that account's address data.", 'Recovery included unmapping Pool Cost Shipment orders, creating reverse JVs for duplicate JVs, resolving a Data set separator-related JV error for KB transmission, and completing Falcon recovery after customer master updates.']
Root Cause: Incomplete or null address fields on the account selected in the Contractor Name field for the NV Quote/Sales Order, including missing city code and Oaza/Common Name, caused the approval-processing error.
Resolution: Implemented NV Quote validation on the Request Approval/Generate Approval action to block processing when the Contractor Name account has incomplete address information, with the message: "Please check the business partner master of the user selected in the business partner name. The customer address in the business partner master is a required field." The fix was validated in UAT and released to PROD on April 14; duplicate JVs were reversed and Falcon recovery was completed.

Investigation reproduced the issue on UAT1 and established that the related NV Sales Order Start Price was set to null during Sub Quote completion. A fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.
Important Findings: ['Parts Internal Order list price is fetched from NV Sales Order.', 'Adding a part through Sub Quote in NV Quote caused the NV Sales Order Start Price to be set to null.', 'The issue was reproduced on UAT1 with NV Sales Order A001293389, part ###600SILVER, resulting in null list price on Parts Internal Order M001293390.', 'When parts are added through Parts and Intenal Work in an NV Quote line item, the list price is displayed; the issue occurred when creating the part order through Sub Quote.', 'The fix was verified on UAT1 using NV Sales Order A001293480 with parts ###600BLACK-5K and ###1003, creating Parts Internal Order M001293481.', 'The fix was applied to PROD in the April 14 release.']
Root Cause: During Sub Quote completion in NV Quote, the Start Price for the added part in NV Sales Order was set to null. Since Parts Internal Order list price is sourced from NV Sales Order, its list price also became null.
Resolution: Fixed the Sub Quote processing issue that set NV Sales Order Start Price to null; the fix was validated on UAT1 and deployed to PROD in the April 14 release.

Root Cause: During data migration, FDP "Previous Assessment Flag" was not set to Y for qualifying orders, leaving prior purchase orders visible in UV Inventory. Users with access to the editable "MF UV Inventory Purchase Order View" could then change the editable "Sales Order #" field without generating a KB Map/Unmap trigger.
Resolution: Recovered migrated orders so prior purchase orders no longer appear in UV Inventory after restock, and changed the "Sales Order #" field to read-only in UV Inventory. The change passed UAT and was released to PROD on March 26, 2025.

Root Cause: FDP did not validate the presence of a JCO during Sales Posting when the Service Quote was not "Customer Approved", allowing Sales Posting without JCO creation or Job Card closure.
Resolution: Implemented a validation in FDP to prevent the missing-JCO Sales Posting scenario; the change was deployed to UAT, approved for Prod, and released to production on March 26, 2025.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: In the Chugoku Production environment, recycle fee orders were not created because the TOB D21F file was received and processed before the corresponding D21A file. D21A creates the chassis order, which is a prerequisite for D21F to create the recycle fee order. The initially reported D21E dependency was corrected: the relevant sequence is D21A and D21F. Affected records were recovered by re-executing D21F after D21A processing; monitoring was implemented to identify similar cases for recovery.
Important Findings: ['The root sequence issue was TOB processing D21F before the corresponding D21A file for the same order.', 'D21A creates the chassis order, while D21F creates the recycle fee order; without the chassis order, D21F cannot create the recycle fee order.', 'The initial reference to D21E in March 2025 was incorrect; the correct prerequisite file is D21A.', 'Re-executing D21F after successful D21A processing created the missing recycle fee orders.', 'The issue was identified as a TOB file sequencing issue rather than a Cubastion Siebel system defect.', 'Monitoring and email notifications were implemented to identify failed, unprocessed, or sequencing-related cases and enable recovery.']
Root Cause: The corresponding TOB D21F file was received and processed before the D21A file. Because D21A had not yet created the prerequisite chassis order, D21F could not create the recycle fee order.
Resolution: Recovered affected records by re-executing D21F after the corresponding D21A process completed, creating the recycle fee orders. Monitoring was implemented to detect similar cases and trigger recovery actions.

Investigation Summary: An intermittent Siebel issue caused Trade-in Consumption Tax not to be correctly reflected in the NV Quote header after entering a Trade-in Amount. Impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered. The code was corrected in UAT and released to production on March 26, 2025, with continued monitoring planned.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurred intermittently and had no specific reproducible steps.', 'The affected behavior occurred when entering a Trade-in Amount: Trade-in Consumption Tax should populate in both the Trade-in subtab and the Quote Header.', 'All impacted records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments were recovered; no recovery was required for other FDP environments.', 'The code did not follow Siebel best practices because Link Specification was not set to TRUE.', 'The UAT validation was intended to confirm that NV quotation and trade-in functionality continued to operate normally after the code change.', 'The production release of the fix was completed on March 26, 2025.']
Root Cause: Link Specification was not set to TRUE in the Siebel code, contrary to Oracle-recommended Siebel best practices, causing intermittent failure to reflect Trade-in Consumption Tax in the NV Quote Header.
Resolution: Set Link Specification to TRUE in UAT, validated that existing NV quotation and trade-in functionality was not impacted, released the fix to production on March 26, 2025, and recovered affected records in the Okayama, Wakayama, and Chugoku environments.

Root Cause: After quote revision, replacement part items were assigned the same line numbers as deleted part items. During quote and order synchronization, they matched existing part items that already had Parts Internal Order and Return order records, leaving the parent order ID unchanged and causing the operation to stop.
Resolution: Recovery was completed for the affected record by removing the parent order ID from the line items associated with the parts; the user was then instructed to create the purchase order.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A bodywork purchase order incorrectly retained the originating sales order's Quote ID when created from a quote containing negative list price and cost. Negative price validation interrupted the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order", causing later quote amendments to synchronize sales-order line items to the bodywork purchase order. A fix was validated across FDP UAT environments and deployed to the production environment on March 12, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced in UAT1 with Bodywork order B001292881 and Sales Order A001292880.', 'A bodywork order item with both negative list price and negative cost triggered the failure path.', 'The "Create Purchase Order" workflow was interrupted by negative price validation.', "The interrupted workflow saved the sales order's Quote ID on the bodywork purchase order.", 'When the quote was amended, line-item synchronization selected all sales orders sharing the Quote ID, including the bodywork purchase order.', 'The fix was applied to all FDP UAT environments and released to the production environment on March 12, 2025.']
Root Cause: Negative price validation broke the workflow triggered by "Create Purchase Order" for a bodywork order with negative cost and list price, causing the sales order's Quote ID to be saved on the bodywork purchase order. Subsequent quote amendments synchronized line items to that bodywork purchase order because it shared the Quote ID.
Resolution: A fix was deployed across all FDP UAT environments and then applied to the production environment in the March 12, 2025 release.

Investigation Summary: UV Quote and UV Sales Order showed differing Sales Profit values after quote creation or revision. Investigation identified inconsistent additional-cost calculation logic and rounding behavior in UV Quote, resulting in profit discrepancies, including 1-yen differences. The UV Quote calculation was aligned with UV Sales Order, validated in UAT-01 for AR#: H000045187, and deployed to production on April 14.
Important Findings: ['Initial UAT validation failed for AR#: H000037289, where Sales Quote# 1-5LHJS7 Rev.2 had Profit 526,340 and SO# E001281570 had Profit 552,740.', 'Data patches were completed in FDP environments except for two records in FDP Okayama; a remaining discrepancy was also reported for FDP Chugoku AR#: H000147553.', 'UV Quote rounded values during Sales Profit calculation, causing profit differences between UV Quote and UV Sales Order.', 'The fix aligned additional cost price calculation logic in UV Quote with UV Sales Order and removed rounding from the UV Quote Profit Amount calculation.', 'The fix is independent of Consumption Tax Rounding configured in Administration – Sales – Consumption Tax Master.', 'UAT passed for the rounding issue on AR#: H000045187 before production deployment.']
Root Cause: UV Quote used different rounding and additional cost price calculation logic than UV Sales Order when calculating Sales Profit, causing inconsistent Profit Amount values.
Resolution: Updated UV Quote Sales Profit calculation to use the same additional cost price logic and no-rounding behavior as UV Sales Order. The change passed UAT-01 validation for AR#: H000045187 and was deployed to production in the April 14 release.

Investigation Summary: A re-edited External WO caused the JV Posting Date for SPO J000192078 to remain at 2025/01/30 while the related work completed on 2025/02/19. Investigation confirmed that the work completion date/time for External WO 1-F9HQT was not updated in the JC Header before JV creation; the JC Header was only updated after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet. A fix was validated in FDP UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on March 12.
Important Findings: ['SPO work start date/time and work completion date/time are sourced from the JC Header.', 'A JV is created when an SPO reaches "Completion of Acceptance Inspection", and its Posting Date is based on the SPO work completion date/time.', 'For re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT, the JC Header retained the previous completion date, causing the JV for SPO J000192078 to use Posting Date 2025/01/30.', 'The JC Header work completion date/time was updated to 2025/02/19 14:05:04 only after Generate Approval was clicked in the MF Job Card Detail Applet.', 'Updating the JC Header after JV creation caused a date/time mismatch between the JV and the SPO screen.', 'The issue was reproduced and fixed in FDP UAT-1 before production deployment.']
Root Cause: The work completion date/time of re-edited External WO 1-F9HQT was not correctly set in the JC Header before the JV was created, so the JV used the prior JC Header/SPO completion date of 2025/01/30.
Resolution: A fix was implemented and validated in FDP UAT-1, then deployed to PROD in the March 12 release.

Investigation Summary: The incident involved missing chassis and option asking prices and costs on the NV Quote. Initial investigation could not reproduce the one-time Production occurrence in UAT, but later testing in RT2 identified pricing issues when the RWD date was removed and re-entered while updating chassis and options. A validation requiring the Desired shipping date before chassis selection was implemented, the error-message wording was corrected, and the fix was released to Production on 12 August 2025.
Important Findings: ['The original Production occurrence was recovered, including the actual cost of options, but could not initially be reproduced in UAT.', 'When the RWD date was null, the selected chassis price was not displayed on the NV Quote.', 'In RT2, removing the RWD date and updating the chassis, then re-adding the date and updating the chassis, resulted in chassis pricing being displayed while option pricing became null.', 'The reported issue concerned missing asking price and cost for both chassis and option prices, not only blank chassis pricing.', 'Backend investigation attributed the zero-cost issue to the selected line options.', 'The validation message was corrected to use "Desired shipping date" rather than "scheduled shipping date".']
Root Cause: A null RWD date caused selected chassis pricing not to display; the zero-cost condition was attributed to the selected line options.
Resolution: Added validation requiring users to enter the Desired shipping date before selecting a chassis, corrected the validation-message wording, and released the changes to Production on 12 August 2025.

Investigation Summary: The recycle-fee submission issue to TOB was caused by duplicate vehicle records with the same recycle fee ticket number. All identified affected records were recovered under MFTBCFFR-3168.
Important Findings: ['The issue occurs when a vehicle is duplicated with the same recycle fee ticket number, preventing correct recycle-fee processing to TOB.', 'Vehicle "BE740G-400580" was initially created in SC Prod from a TCB01 file with both Fuso reception # and VIN# set to "046754".', 'The vehicle was migrated to FDP Chugoku before D21A from TOB updated its VIN# to "BE740G-400580".', 'During vehicle delta-data migration, the import program treated the updated VIN# as a user key and created a new vehicle record.', 'The user submitted the recycle fee to TOB before the duplicate-vehicle recovery was completed.', 'All impacted records, not only the reported order, were recovered as part of MFTBCFFR-3168.']
Root Cause: A vehicle was migrated while its VIN# was "046754", then D21A updated the VIN# to "BE740G-400580". During subsequent vehicle delta-data migration, the import program used VIN# as its user key and created a duplicate vehicle record.
Resolution: Recovered all identified impacted duplicate-vehicle records under MFTBCFFR-3168, including the reported order.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A Sales Price mismatch between Siebel and FDP PBI reports was traced to ODI logic handling Billing Rate Type values. The logic did not correctly recognize the labor product 'FDP Rate' for FDP Shikoku order I00006001, causing the Sales Price to differ between Siebel and PBI. The ODI logic was corrected, validated in FDP UAT5 using order I000035271, and released to production in the FDP release on February 8, 2025.
Important Findings: ['The incident involved mismatched Sales Price values between Siebel and the FDP PBI report.', "For FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001, line item 1-1A8DK0 had labor product 'FDP Rate', which did not satisfy the ODI Sales Price logic.", "The ODI logic was expected to include 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', but incorrect values such as 'FDP???' and '?????????' were observed.", 'Recovery was completed for the affected mismatched values, after which Siebel sales prices matched the PBI report.', "The corrected logic was verified in FDP UAT5 with ORDER_NUM I000035271 and labor product 'FDP Rate'; values populated correctly in FDP PBI reports.", 'The ODI change was released to production with the FDP release on February 8, 2025.']
Root Cause: ODI Sales Price logic did not correctly match the Billing Rate Type value 'FDP Rate' due to incorrect expected values, so the labor product on FDP Shikoku Order_num I00006001 was excluded from Sales Price processing.
Resolution: Modified the ODI logic in FDP UAT to correctly handle 'FDP Rate' and 'Warranty Rate', validated the fix in FDP UAT5, recovered the affected mismatched data, and deployed the change to production on February 8, 2025.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: In UV Purchase Quote, the List Applet fetched Assessment number from Vehicle while the Form Applet fetched it from Assessment Request (AR). When a new Assessment Request was created for the same VIN#, the Vehicle Assessment number was updated and older Purchase Quotes displayed the newer number in the List Applet. The fix aligned both applets to fetch Assessment # from AR, was validated in UAT01, and released to production on February 12, 2025.
Important Findings: ['UV Purchase Quotes created from different Assessment numbers but linked to the same VIN# could display an updated Assessment number in the List Applet.', 'The List Applet sourced Assessment number from Vehicle, whereas the Form Applet sourced it from Assessment Request (AR).', 'Creating a new Assessment Request for the same Vehicle updated the Vehicle Assessment number, affecting older Purchase Quotes linked to that Vehicle.', 'The reported behavior initially matched the SC version existing functionality.', 'The fix was tested on UAT01 using UV Purchase Quote 1-5WJ1LD and UAT passed.', 'The change was released to production on February 12, 2025.']
Root Cause: Inconsistent Assessment number sourcing between the UV Purchase Quote List Applet (Vehicle) and Form Applet (Assessment Request); Vehicle Assessment number updates for the same VIN# changed the value shown for older Purchase Quotes.
Resolution: Changed the List Applet to fetch Assessment # from AR, matching the Form Applet; validated in UAT01 and deployed to production.

Investigation Summary: Sales Posting JV amounts and creation behavior for outsourcing orders were inconsistent with the required IBOS and Non-IBOS pricing logic. The existing logic depended on Net Price, causing JV creation to fail when Net Price was absent despite bodywork and other billing amounts being present. The UAT1 fix changed Sales Posting JV creation to evaluate Net Price and Total Selling Price, with the Base Amount set to their sum; the change was validated and released to Prod on 14 May 2025.
Important Findings: ['Initially, JV contained Agency Fee, PO, and CT pricing, while the invoice sent Agency Price plus Total Selling and did not send PO price, causing a JV-to-invoice price difference.', 'For Non-IBOS cases, Total Selling Price was mapped to JV in UAT1; subsequent changes addressed both IBOS and Non-IBOS logic.', 'Outsourcing Order A001292536 did not create a Sales Posting JV because Net Price was not set in Taxes & Expenses and the existing creation condition required Net Price to be non-zero.', 'The required behavior was to create a JV when bodywork and other billing amounts were present, regardless of whether Net Price was set.', 'The corrected Sales Posting JV Base Amount is Net Price plus Total Selling Price.', 'JV tax calculation subtracts License Plate Number Fee and Illuminated License Plate Number Fee from the taxable amount; the validated example calculated tax of 5200 from a taxable amount of 52000 at a 10% Consumption Tax Rate.']
Root Cause: Sales Posting JV creation and Base Amount logic relied on Net Price being non-zero, so no JV was created when Net Price was absent even when Total Selling Price or bodywork and other billing amounts required a JV.
Resolution: Updated the Sales Posting JV condition to check Net Price and Total Selling Price, and set the JV Base Amount to the sum of Net Price and Total Selling Price. The fix was validated in UAT1 and released to Prod in the 14 May 2025 release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A mismatch between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was reproduced on UAT-4 using two browser sessions. Completing the Shaken Expense in one browser created a Journal Voucher using the original Actual Amount, while a stale second browser session could subsequently overwrite the Actual Expense amount. The fix prevents updates to Actual Amount after the Actual Expense is Completed, and the Journal Voucher difference was recovered.
Important Findings: ['The issue was reproduced on UAT-4 with JC# I000031108 and Expense ID 1-JCL44.', 'Clicking Done in Browser 1 marked the Shaken Expense as Completed and created a Journal Voucher with Actual Amount 17,400.', 'Without refreshing Browser 2, changing Weight Tax Actual Amount to 16,800 overwrote the Actual Expense but did not update the existing Journal Voucher.', 'The resulting discrepancy between Actual Expense and Journal Voucher was ▲600.', 'After the fix, users cannot update Actual Amount from another browser once the Actual Expense is Completed.']
Root Cause: A stale multi-browser session allowed the Actual Expense Actual Amount to be updated after the record was marked Completed and its Journal Voucher had already been created, causing the Journal Voucher and Actual Expense amounts to diverge.
Resolution: Implemented a UAT-4 restriction preventing Actual Amount updates in multi-browser sessions after Actual Expense status is Completed, and added the ▲600 difference to the Journal Voucher.

Important Findings: ['For SO M000034005 in UAT-5, setting Already Returned Qty in the shipment screen equal to the ordered quantity caused return-order creation to fail.', 'The displayed validation was "Please enter Return Qty."', 'After the validation, the Already Returned Qty on the Parts Sales Order screen was updated with the value entered in the shipment screen.', 'The issue was also reproduced for M000031415 in UAT5, while testing with several other orders did not reproduce it.', 'Previously affected shipment-line Already Returned Qty values were reset to 0 for SO M000003330 and M000007642 to allow Parts Sales return recreation.', 'The corrective change made Already Returned Qty read-only in the shipment screen.']
Root Cause: Already Returned Qty was editable in the shipment screen; entering a value equal to the ordered quantity propagated that value to the Parts Sales Order screen and prevented Parts Sales return creation.
Resolution: Made the Already Returned Qty field read-only in the shipment screen, verified the fix in FDP UAT-1, and released it in the 23 January 2025 FDP release.

Root Cause: Manual recovery for MFTBCFFR-2834 updated vehicle information in the Sales Order but omitted the related Body Building Order, causing inconsistent vehicle information and the Delivery Request Approval error.
Resolution: Updated the Recovery Manual so vehicle information is updated for all related orders during recovery; associated orders were subsequently validated to have consistent Vehicle IDs across all production environments.

Root Cause: A WO was added when the JC status was "Maintenance Completed", so the added WO was not included in the last WO date update.
Resolution: Modified the JC header [Approval Request] action to update the date of the last WO including added WOs; the change was verified in UAT-1 and deployed to PROD on February 26, 2025.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Changing a quote to customer approved failed because the customer code used in the Job card had a null tax exempt flag. The tax exempt flag is non-nullable in Service order BC, causing the error during the quote status change. Recovery was performed to allow the user to proceed, and a fix to default null tax exempt flag values to 'N' was validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on December 16.
Important Findings: ['The failure occurred when setting the quote status to customer approved.', 'The customer code used in the Job card had a null tax exempt flag value.', 'Tax exempt flag is a non-nullable column in Service order BC.', "The corrective logic updates the tax exempt flag to 'N' when it is null for a customer.", 'The fix was validated in UAT-1 for JC# I001286847 and Quote# 1-5O8YM8.', 'The approved fix was released to Production in the December 16 release.']
Root Cause: The customer code associated with the Job card had a null tax exempt flag, which violated the non-nullable tax exempt flag column requirement in Service order BC during quote approval.
Resolution: Updated the tax exempt flag to 'N' when it is null for a customer; the fix was validated in UAT-1 and released to Production on December 16.

Investigation Summary: The FVP flag in Material Master was being set to null for all parts received in the Material Master file. Investigation found that an FVP flag mapping existed even though D2S did not provide the FVP flag in the Material Master file. The mapping was inactivated in FDP UAT and then released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['D2S does not provide the FVP flag in the Material Master file.', 'An existing Material Master mapping for the FVP flag caused the FVP flag to be set to null for all incoming parts.', 'The FVP flag mapping was inactivated in FDP UAT.', 'The change was released to Prod.']
Root Cause: A Material Master mapping expected an FVP flag value that was not provided by D2S, causing the FVP flag to be set to null for all parts in the Material Master file.
Resolution: Inactivated the FVP flag mapping in FDP UAT and released the change to Prod.

Investigation Summary: For Body Building Order B000160867, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created because the order amount was 0 after the line item was cancelled. The Consumption Tax field retained tax calculated before cancellation because it is a column-based field and is not updated when a line item is cancelled. This behavior was confirmed as expected, and the incident was closed without a corrective change.
Important Findings: ['Body Building Order B000160867 had an order amount of 0 because its line item was cancelled.', 'Journal Voucher Lines for PO and its Consumption Tax were not created when the order amount was 0.', 'The Consumption Tax field stores the total tax from line-item amounts when amounts are entered.', 'Consumption Tax is not updated when a line item is cancelled because it is a column-based field.', "Body Building Orders with cancelled line items can still have the status 'Acceptance Verification Done'."]
Root Cause: The line item for Body Building Order B000160867 was cancelled, causing the order amount to become 0; therefore, Journal Voucher Lines for PO and Consumption Tax were not created.
Resolution: No system correction was required; the behavior was explained as expected and the Jira was closed.

Investigation Summary: Address changes made in Basic Info/Customer information were not consistently synchronized to AR/AP and Quote BIP. Root Cause: User D8KOUSTA had Branch-CS-Staff configured as the primary position instead of Branch NV/UV Sales Staff, while approval rules use the requester’s primary position.
Resolution: Reverted the Assessment Request to "In Progress" and instructed the user to set Branch NV/UV Sales Staff as the primary position before selecting "Generate Approval".

Investigation Summary: The incident concerned Tax/Non-Tax Flag and Tax Rate synchronization in the Quote/JCO Header when the customer was changed in the JC Header in FDP UAT1. The issue was fixed and validated in UAT-1 using new JCs I001281065 and I001281069. The change was subsequently released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['Initial synchronization of Flag and Tax Value in the Quote Header was corrected in FDP UAT1.', 'Changing the customer in the JC Header from TAX to Non TAX, or from Non TAX to TAX, did not update the Flag in the Quote Header.', 'In the SC version, the TAX Flag remained correctly linked when the customer was changed.', 'After the fix, the Non-Tax Flag and Tax Rate values in the Quote/JCO Header were correct for JC I001281065 and Quote 1-5KJ6FX.', 'Customer update behavior was validated for JC I001281069 with Account Code 0000B18463.']
Root Cause: The Tax/Non-Tax Flag linkage from the JC Header customer change to the Quote Header was not updating correctly in FDP UAT1.
Resolution: Fixed the tax flag linkage with customer changes in UAT1, validated the Quote/JCO Header values, and released the change to Prod.

Investigation Summary: The "Submit to TOB" button was inactive for a Chassis Order because its selected model code had Product Line "Bus". The implemented logic, consistent with SC, enables the button only for Product Line "Truck". Recovery was completed by changing the Product Line of model code "BG740GBAGG-5" to "Truck", after which the button became active.
Important Findings: ['"Submit to TOB" is active only for model codes with Product Line "Truck".', 'The affected Chassis Order used a model code with Product Line "Bus", causing the button to remain inactive.', 'SC contains the same logic and the same model code was also classified as Product Line "Bus" in SC.', 'Product Line for model code "BG740GBAGG-5" was updated to "Truck".', 'After the Product Line update, the "Submit to TOB" button became active and recovery was completed.']
Root Cause: The affected model code was configured with Product Line "Bus", while the implemented "Submit to TOB" logic enables the button only for Product Line "Truck".
Resolution: Updated the Product Line of model code "BG740GBAGG-5" from "Bus" to "Truck", which activated the "Submit to TOB" button.

Resolution: Recovered the data in prod so Recycle Fee data displayed correctly, and added a recovery step to not open additional files present in the Inbound folder.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Trade-In synchronization created UV Purchase Orders when revised and approved quotes synchronized to sales orders that were not in an appropriate status. In the NV flow, this occurred after an NV Sales Order approval was rejected; in the UV flow, it occurred while the UV Sales Order remained Pending. The issue was fixed in UAT1, validated with test sales orders, and released to Production in the 13 September FDP release.
Important Findings: ['Revision 2 of NV Quote# 1-UJYUK synchronized after approval and generated PO# F000110671 although the associated order# A000109884 had been rejected.', 'The Trade-In synchronization process did not account for an NV Sales Order in Rejected status.', 'For NV Quotes, revising and approving a quote after rejecting the generated NV Sales Order triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In.', 'For UV Quotes, revising and approving a quote triggered creation of a UV Purchase Order for the Trade-In while the UV Sales Order remained Pending.', 'The fix was validated in UAT1 using NV SO#A001268431 and UV SO#E001268440 before Production deployment.']
Root Cause: Trade-In synchronization generated UV Purchase Orders without properly accounting for the status of the associated sales order, including NV Sales Orders in Rejected status and UV Sales Orders in Pending status.
Resolution: The issue was fixed in UAT1 and released to Production in the 13 September FDP release.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A Delivery Request creation error occurred when purchase orders associated with a vehicle were not all mapped. Investigation found that a previously cancelled assessment for the same vehicle set a flag to 'Y' on all mapped POs; this flag was handled during sales order mapping but was not checked during Delivery Request creation. The Delivery Request logic was corrected, validated in UAT1 on AR# H000030031, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ["A cancelled assessment sets a flag to 'Y' for all POs mapped to the associated vehicle.", 'For a subsequent assessment with the same VIN#, only the newest purchase orders are mapped in the sales order.', 'Delivery Request creation did not check the cancellation-related PO flag, causing the error that all purchase orders were not mapped.', 'The condition was fixed for Delivery Request creation and deployed to UAT1.', 'UAT passed on AR# H000030031, and the fix was released to Prod.']
Root Cause: Delivery Request creation did not check the 'Y' flag set on POs mapped to a vehicle when a prior assessment was cancelled, resulting in validation that all purchase orders were not mapped.
Resolution: Updated Delivery Request creation logic to check the cancellation-related PO flag; the change passed UAT1 validation and was released to Prod.

Investigation Summary: The incident concerned missing responsible/collector information on the accounts receivable update screen. Root Cause: The responsible information was not displayed because "Module open Flag NV" was unchecked; this intentionally nulls and makes the NV Responsible values read-only.
Resolution: Implemented changes were validated in UAT-1 and released to Prod; users must set "Module open Flag NV" to True during "Update AR" to display NV responsible details.

Investigation Summary: An additional field introduced during the JCT CR Release was removed from UAT1 because it was no longer required. Root Cause: The Service Request was created by UserID D8FORF19 with Position Type HQ-Gn-Affairs-GMgr, which does not trigger the Approval Flow. The existing functionality requires a creator with Position Type Branch-Parts-Staff for the Service Request status to change to Completed.
Resolution: Removed the no-longer-required additional field, validated Service Request completion in UAT-1 using a Branch-Parts-Staff user, and released the incident to Prod.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The "Last DB Refresh Time" in the Okayama Power BI UAT report remained at the previous successful load time despite daytime report refreshes. Investigation found that the 12:00 PM ODI Load plan failed because duplicate database data was not permitted at an ODI processing step. The Load plan issue was fixed and monitored successfully for three days, after which daytime Power BI refreshes displayed the correct "Last DB Refresh Time".
Important Findings: ['The Power BI report refresh itself could complete while "Last DB Refresh Time" continued to show the last successful ODI daily Load plan run.', 'The 12:00 PM ODI Load plan failure was caused by duplicate data in the database that was not permitted at an ODI step.', 'The 21:30 Load plan run completed successfully after the duplicate-data issue was resolved.', 'The Load plan for UAT Okayama was fixed and ran successfully for three days during monitoring.', 'Scheduled Power BI refresh failures requiring manual refresh were identified as a separate issue tracked in MFTBCFFR-2274.']
Root Cause: Duplicate data in the database caused the 12:00 PM ODI Load plan to fail at a step where duplicates were not permitted, preventing "Last DB Refresh Time" from being updated.
Resolution: The UAT Okayama Load plan issue was fixed, the successful load runs updated "Last DB Refresh Time" correctly in daytime Power BI report refreshes, and the fix was monitored successfully for three days.

Investigation Summary: No employee was assigned to the Branch-CS-Head position in Division 10, causing no user to appear for that role in approval flow history. Analysis of the April 1, 2024 employee master execution on Prod found that Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, so D8TMASAA received the Branch-Service-Mgr role instead. Important Findings: ['D8ISHDA1 was assigned to the Branch-Head position, not the Branch-CS-Head position, in Okayama Higashi Branch with 10 Dealer Code.', 'The April 1, 2024 employee master file execution removed D8TOTAKE from the Branch-CS-Head position and intended to assign D8TMASAA.', 'The employee master file operation for D8TMASAA was specified as "Assign" although the investigation stated it should have been "Change".', 'Position Type Mapping mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr, resulting in D8TMASAA being assigned Branch-Service-Mgr rather than Branch-CS-Head.', 'Because no employee held Branch-CS-Head in Division 10, no user appeared for that role in approval flow history.']
Root Cause: Position Type Mapping incorrectly mapped Branch-CS-Head to Branch-Service-Mgr during employee master processing, leaving no employee assigned to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.
Resolution: Corrected the position mapping on Prod and re-executed the employee master file for D8TMASAA, which correctly assigned the user to Branch-CS-Head in Division 10.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders was not correctly sourced after SC SIEBEL changes to "Change Order Completion Date/Time". Investigation found that the SC Siebel changes under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel, requiring an AMS CR on the FDP Okayama Siebel side and a corresponding FDP PBI mapping update. The fix was validated in FDP UAT and deployed to FDP PROD on July 20, 2024.
Important Findings: ['SC SIEBEL changes for "Change Order Completion Date/Time" under AMS CR 610008113 were not reflected in FDP Siebel.', 'FDP PBI Settlement Date for change orders needed to source the "Change Order Completion date" column from Siebel.', 'An AMS CR was required for FDP Okayama Siebel in addition to the PBI change.', 'The PROD release added a new column to the ODI mapping and required a full load of Daily Load Plan.', 'The fix was verified in FDP UAT for reports SV_101, 1_10A, 1_12A, and 1_15A, and the issue could not be reproduced in UAT after the change.']
Root Cause: The "Change Order Completion Date/Time" changes made in SC SIEBEL were not reflected in FDP Siebel, so FDP PBI could not source the correct Settlement Date for change orders.
Resolution: Applied the required FDP Okayama Siebel AMS CR and updated the FDP PBI ODI mapping to source change-order Settlement Date from the Siebel "Change Order Completion date" column; performed a full Daily Load Plan load and deployed the fix to FDP PROD.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: PBI 1_10A Report populated Settlement Date from the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date, causing dates to appear for Change Orders that were still in progress. Analysis confirmed that the PBI logic differs from Siebel, where the relevant field is Change Order Completion date and only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date. A change to PBI SV_1_10A was identified as necessary, and an AMS-CR was requested.
Important Findings: ['The settlement date in PBI was populated using the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date.', 'For JC# I000097002 / Change Order# K000121869, LAST_UPD changed from March 18 to March 19 after an update, and PBI reflected March 19.', 'Using LAST_UPD causes in-progress Change Orders, including recently created and unapproved Change Orders, to receive a settlement date in PBI.', 'Siebel uses Change Order Completion date for the settlement date requirement.', 'Only approved Change Orders should have a settlement date and be displayed in PBI reports.', 'PBI SV_1_10A requires logic changes to align with Siebel.']
Root Cause: PBI 1_10A mapped Settlement Date to the Service Change Order LAST_UPD date instead of the Siebel Change Order Completion date, resulting in settlement dates for in-progress, unapproved Change Orders.
Resolution: An AMS-CR was requested to implement Settlement Date logic changes in PBI SV_1_10A to align with Siebel and populate settlement dates only for approved Change Orders.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The incident concerned changing Adjustment Amount values in Siebel. Directly changing and saving the Adjustment Amount on an existing record was identified as an incorrect operation. Users must end-date the old record and create a new record with the revised amount and corresponding effective dates.
Important Findings: ['Directly changing and saving Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record is an incorrect operation.', 'The old record must have its Effective To date populated before the Adjustment Amount is changed.', 'A new record must be created for the revised Adjustment Amount.', 'The new record must have the appropriate Effective From date populated.', 'The required handling was classified as an operation rule rather than a system issue.']
Root Cause: Users attempted to directly change and save Adjustment Amount on an existing Siebel record instead of end-dating the old record and creating a new effective-dated record.
Resolution: Users were instructed to populate Effective To on the old record, then create a new record with the updated Adjustment Amount and an appropriate Effective From date.

Root Cause: The code validation condition allowed only "Acceptance Verification Done" for Body Building Orders, but the IBOS Body Building Order was in "Shipped" status.
Resolution: Updated the Body Building (IBOS) order condition to include "Shipped" status and implemented the change in UAT1.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Purchase type values were incorrect or null in PBI reports because of both report LOV inconsistencies and a Siebel assessment update defect. In Siebel, Assessment purpose remained editable after an assessment reached "Assessment Completed"; cancelling a purpose change with Esc could leave the associated purchase type as null. The fix was validated in UAT1, released to Prod, and affected Prod records were recovered; the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was subsequently rectified.
Important Findings: ['UV_2B had different LOVs between PBI and SIEBEL, causing purchase-type discrepancies for records H000000801, H000002802, and H000003406.', 'UV_2_01_2_02 did not display a value in the SIEBEL UI, so the value was not reflected in the PBI report.', 'Assessment purpose was editable when assessment status was "Assessment Completed".', 'If a user began changing Assessment purpose and pressed Esc to restore the prior value, the UI restored the purpose but set the assessment purchase type to null.', 'UAT initially showed "UV Trade-in" for purchase classifications in 2-01, 2-02, 2-05, 2-06, and 2-01(History), rather than "Magotori".', 'After the Prod release, the Purchase Type filter in 2-01 and 2-02 incorrectly included "SV reception category" LOV values; this was rectified.']
Root Cause: In Siebel, Assessment purpose could be edited after an assessment was "Assessment Completed". Cancelling an in-progress Assessment purpose change with Esc restored the displayed purpose but left the associated purchase type set to null. Separate PBI and SIEBEL LOV differences also caused UV_2B purchase-type discrepancies.
Resolution: The issue was fixed and validated in UAT1, then released to Prod. Affected Prod records were recovered, PBI reports were refreshed, and the Purchase Type filter LOV issue was rectified.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A deleted line item in UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) caused a line-number mismatch between the quote and the UV Sales Order created through the auto order button. During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), the mismatch deleted order line items and child records, causing the sync to fail when updating Line Item# 5. The corrective change disabled deletion from the Line Items tab while retaining deletion of Liability Insurance through the Taxes and Expenses tab; the change was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD.
Important Findings: ['Deleting Line Item# 4, Expense (S07), from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) removed Line Item# 4 from the Backend Column.', 'The UV Sales Order created through the auto order button still contained Line Item# 4 for Recycle Fee(YN5Z).', 'During synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3), Line Item# 4 and its child records were deleted from the order, which also deleted Line Item# 5.', 'The sync failed when UV Sales Quote Line Item# 5 attempted to update the already deleted UV Sales Order Line Item# 5.', 'The FDP fix disables the Delete button on the Line Items tab; Liability Insurance can only be deleted from the Taxes and Expenses tab.', 'The change passed UAT1 validation and was implemented on PROD.']
Root Cause: Deletion of Line Item# 4 from UV Sales Quote (Revision 1) created a Backend Column line-number mismatch with the UV Sales Order, which retained Line Item# 4 after auto-order creation. Synchronization of UV Sales Quote (Revision 3) then deleted order lines and child records, including Line Item# 5, causing the subsequent Line Item# 5 update to fail.
Resolution: Disabled the Delete button on the Line Items tab and restricted deletion of Liability Insurance to the Taxes and Expenses tab. The change was implemented in UAT1, passed UAT, and was deployed to PROD.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Rejected and incomplete used-car sales orders appeared in reports because users manually populated date fields used by report filters. UV SO# E000087121 appeared in the Order Report despite Rejected status because Approval Date was manually entered; UV SO# E000037797 appeared in the sales report because Delivery Completion Approved Date was manually entered. The incident was classified as user misoperation and closed with no system fix required.
Important Findings: ['Approval Date is normally auto-populated when an approver approves a Sales Order, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000087121 before approval was requested.', 'The Order Report filters approved orders based on Approval Date, so UV SO# E000087121 appeared even after rejection by the Branch Head.', 'Delivery Completion Approved Date is normally populated when the Delivery Request is completed, but it was manually entered for UV SO# E000037797.', 'The Sales Order Reporting screen filters sales-posting-completed orders based on Delivery Completion Approved Date, causing UV SO# E000037797 to appear in the sales report.', 'Making the two date fields Read Only was confirmed as possible and not expected to affect functionality, but no change was implemented because the issue was handled through user operation.']
Root Cause: User misoperation: manual entry of Approval Date and Delivery Completion Approved Date caused orders to satisfy date-based report filters regardless of their actual approval or delivery-completion status.
Resolution: No system fix was implemented. The incident was handled through user operation and the Jira was rejected/closed.
