Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: BIP generation failed because the Tax Rate column in NV Sales Order was set to null. The Generate Approval logic queried Consumption Tax Master using the Sales Order Last Contract Date for FDP-Okayama orders with an acknowledgment date earlier than the current date; no matching tax-master record was found. The Consumption Tax Master start date was changed in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version, allowing tax percent to be set correctly.
Important Findings: ['Tax percent in Sales Order originates from the sales quote but is recalculated by logic behind the Generate Approval button.', 'For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the logic queries Consumption Tax Master using Start Date <= Last Contract Date <= End Date.', 'In FDP-Okayama, the acknowledgment date was 2020/11/30 and affected orders had a Last Contract Date earlier than the Consumption Tax Master start date of 2023/07/29.', 'The Consumption Tax Master query returned zero records, causing tax percent and the NV Sales Order Tax Rate column to be set to null.', 'The same behavior was reproduced in SC UAT1 using Order A025013709 with Last Contract Date 2018/01/31 earlier than Start Date 2020/11/30, resulting in Order Sheet BIP failure.', 'The logic was confirmed to be the same as in SC.']
Root Cause: The Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama was later than the affected Sales Order Last Contract Date. For acknowledgment dates earlier than today, the Generate Approval logic queried tax records by Last Contract Date and returned no result, setting tax percent to null and causing BIP generation failure.
Resolution: Changed the Consumption Tax Master start date in FDP-Okayama Prod to match the SC version: 2019/10/01.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: For PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS, the Journal Voucher account item code was determined using the Vehicle product class derived from VIN. When VIN was null, the product class defaulted to Others and selected the class-Others account item code. The logic was changed to fetch the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen, validated in Uat, and released to Prod.
Important Findings: ['The original logic fetched the Vehicle product class from VIN.', 'When VIN was null, the product class was set to Others.', 'The Others product class caused the Journal Voucher for PO - Body Building Order - Non IBOS to use the class-Others account item code.', 'The corrected logic fetches the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen.', 'The fix was tested in Uat, approved after validation, and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: The Vehicle product class was derived from VIN; when VIN was null, it defaulted to Others, resulting in selection of the class-Others account item code in the Journal Voucher.
Resolution: Updated the logic to fetch the Vehicle Product Class from the Sales Order Screen instead of VIN, then tested it in Uat and released it to Prod.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The Parts Quote estimation action failed because the user set the record Active flag to N before attempting estimation. An inactive record cannot be updated, so the status could not change and the system displayed "The record in not editable". The behavior was confirmed in UAT1 and is existing functionality consistent with SC; the incident was rejected as no product defect was identified.
Important Findings: ['Parts sub-quotes created from the NV sub-quotes screen have a null branch Id, so no branch name is displayed on the Parts Quote screen.', 'Setting the Active flag to N makes the Parts Quote record inactive and non-editable.', 'The Estimate button cannot update an inactive record; therefore, the Parts Quote status does not change.', 'With the Active flag set to Y, the estimation process works correctly.', 'The behavior was replicated and confirmed in UAT1 and is consistent with SC.']
Root Cause: The user set the Parts Quote Active flag to N before estimation, making the record inactive and preventing the Estimate action from updating its status.
Resolution: Set the Active flag to Y before clicking the Estimate button. No system change was required; the incident was rejected as expected business functionality.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Approval routing for Quote and Job Card was using the total of all Non-chargeable costs when a Free Cost line item was present, causing approval escalation up to HQ for JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71. The required logic was to evaluate only the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the applicable line item type: 42 (Free Cost) or 45 (Reworking). Separate total fields were created, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.
Important Findings: ['For JC I000049866 / Quote 1-MDQ71, the presence of a Free Cost line item caused all Non-chargable values to be summed to 19190, exceeding the 10000 approval threshold.', 'The approval flow must use Non Chargeable Cost Total for Line Item Type 42 only when Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) exists.', 'The same line-item-specific calculation logic is required for Line Item Type 45 (Reworking).', 'The existing configuration behaved the same in UAT and required both Siebel configuration and approval flow changes.', 'New Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields were created for Line Item Type 42 and Line Item Type 45 and used for Quote and Job Card approver selection.', 'FDP UAT-1 confirmed that approvers were judged using only the Free Cost total before PROD deployment.']
Root Cause: The approval rule summed all Non-chargable costs whenever a Free Cost line item was present, rather than calculating and using the Non Chargeable Cost Total for the relevant line item type only.
Resolution: Created separate Total of Non-chargeable Cost fields for Line Item Type 42 (Free Cost) and Line Item Type 45 (Reworking), updated Quote and Job Card approver selection to use the applicable line-item-specific total, validated in FDP UAT-1, and deployed to PROD on 9th April.

Root Cause: The KB interface logic did not restrict outbound records to employee-master updates and did not select the latest updated record when employee codes were duplicated.
Resolution: Updated the KB interface so it sends affected records only when the employee master is updated and selects the latest updated record for duplicate employee codes; tested in UAT and deployed to Prod on December 15.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Recovery data for September and October required correction before release to Prod. Validation found that BZDO008 was generated using D/N price * Qty for price revision, while KB processes price revision and cycle count with the same logic. The UAT fix changed BZDO008 generation for both workflows and was validated before release to Prod.
Important Findings: ['BZDO008 initially showed D/N price * Qty for price revision data.', 'KB processes cycle count and price revision using the same logic.', 'BZDO008 must contain D/N price only for both cycle count and price revision.', 'Records must not be created when D/N price is 0, because they cause an error on the KB side.', 'Price revision recovery data must use the same Posting date for all records; September 30 data must not include an October 1 Posting date.', 'The fix was completed and tested in UAT, approved, and released to Prod.']
Root Cause: BZDO008 generation for price revision used D/N price * Qty and allowed records with D/N price of 0, which was incompatible with the shared KB processing logic used for cycle count and price revision.
Resolution: Updated the UAT and Prod program for both cycle count and price revision so BZDO008 is created with D/N price only, records with D/N price of 0 are not created, and recovery-data Posting dates are consistent across records. The change was tested in UAT and released to Prod.

Investigation Summary: Creating a "Payer Change" Change Order in FDP failed at Generate Approval with "Please Enter the Value For Payer Finance Account Code". Root Cause: Backend account validation configuration migrated from SC required a Payer Finance Account Code during Generate Approval, although FDP did not have the corresponding Payer account configuration/value.
Resolution: Updated Service Quote creation to copy the Bill To Customer field into the Payer field. The change was tested in UAT1, approved, and deployed to Prod.

An ODI Package filter was implemented and validated in UAT and PROD to exclude cancelled work order status; historical JC values were provided in an Excel recovery file.
Important Findings: ['Actual Labour Hour was incorrectly summarized in Power BI, while the corresponding SC (1-10 report) column was not summarized.', 'Removing the Power BI aggregation corrected the initial discrepancy and did not require data recovery because values were recalculated using the revised logic.', 'The 1-10A report and SC PBI included labour hours from cancelled work orders, including JC I000013477 and JC I022120457.', 'An ODI Package filter was added to exclude work orders with cancelled status.', 'The ODI filter affected JCs updated after implementation; earlier JCs required corresponding DB_LAST_UPD updates for recalculation.', 'UAT validation using JCs I001235533 and I001235538 confirmed that cancelled work order labour hours were excluded from PBI.']
Root Cause: The ODI Package did not filter out cancelled work order status, causing cancelled work order labour hours to be included in Actual Labour Hour calculations. The initial discrepancy was additionally caused by aggregation of the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI.
Resolution: Removed aggregation from the Actual Labour Hour column in Power BI and deployed an ODI Package filter in PROD on 13-OCT-2023 to exclude cancelled work orders. An Excel file was provided with updated and previous Actual Labor Hour values for earlier JCs.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: The NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync excluded cases where a revised quote was created before Sales Posting, allowing quote changes to remain linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed. An AMS-CR was implemented for NV and UV to handle revised quotes created before Sales Posting, including cancellation, active/sub-quote reassignment, and validation for pending approvals. The change was validated on UAT1, including a corrected UV rejection-status case, and released to PROD on 5 December.
Important Findings: ['The original sync logic ignored Sales Order sync when the 3rd revised quote was created before NV SO Sales Order.', 'Revised quotes created before Sales Posting could allow edits to Model Code, option, color, and tire while linked to a Sales Order with Sales Posting Completed.', 'For In Progress or Rejected quotes created before Sales Posting, Delivery Completion approval must cancel the quote and move the active flag and only sub quotes created in the previous revision to the Sales Posting-synced quote revision.', 'For Pending Approval quotes created before Sales Posting, approval generation or Delivery Completion Approval must show: "There is a correction request request for approval for this order, please check."', 'During UAT1 validation, UV Quote 1-431G92 rev.5 remained Rejected after Sales Posting; this was resolved and retested with SO E001239841 and Quote 1-43BOUX.', 'Impacted NV and UV data was extracted after the PROD release for recovery through SRs where applicable.']
Root Cause: NV Quote to NV Sales Order Sync was conditioned on whether a revised quote was created before or after Sales Posting, causing sync processing to be skipped for revised quotes created before Sales Posting.
Resolution: Released an AMS-CR for NV and UV that syncs all NV SO Sales Posting Completed cases regardless of revised-quote creation timing; it cancels applicable In Progress/Rejected quotes, updates active flags and prior-revision sub quotes, and blocks Pending Approval quotes with a validation error. The UV UAT1 status-handling defect was corrected before PROD release.

Investigation Summary: The incident involved incorrect or ambiguous part-number handling for Parts PO#: N000013519 when allocations changed. Resolution: Implemented an AMS CR that adds a D2S Allocation creation timestamp tag and processes allocations according to the D2S Timestamp; released to Okayama Prod. on 25th June.

Root Cause: The UV Sales Order map-button logic did not exclude Parts Sales Orders already mapped to the selected Purchase Order, allowing a Parts Sales Order to be mapped to a UV Sales Order when both used the same VIN.

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: A cancelled Assessment record required recovery after the vehicle was restocked. The Assessment Request vehicle-value update depends on a change to the UV Inventory vehicle value. Because UV Inventory already contained the same value, 1,034,500, no inventory update occurred and the downstream Assessment Request update was not triggered. Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered, and the proposed recovery approach was to null the UV Inventory vehicle value before recovery.
Important Findings: ['The issue could not be replicated in UAT1 or RT2, and other Assessment Requests worked correctly in PROD.', 'Vehicle H000000001 was restocked and cancelled through SR#MFTBCFFR-1637.', 'The workflow is: Assessment Request Stock in Verification Completed; UV Inventory vehicle value updated from UV Purchase Order; Assessment Request vehicle value updated from the UV Inventory update.', 'UV Inventory already held vehicle value 1,034,500 after Assessment #H000000001 completed a re-evaluation request with the same value.', 'Because the UV Inventory value did not change, the downstream Assessment Request update trigger did not execute.', 'Assessment Number H000000037 was recovered with Vehicle Value 1,034,500.']
Root Cause: UV Inventory already contained vehicle value 1,034,500, so the update from UV Purchase Order produced no value change and did not trigger the downstream Assessment Request vehicle-value update during recovery of a cancelled Assessment.
Resolution: Recovered Assessment Number H000000037 with Vehicle Value 1,034,500. For cancelled-Assessment recovery cases, add a recovery step to set the UV Inventory vehicle value to null so the subsequent update triggers the Assessment Request update.

Root Cause: Flapping of the track associated with the IP route caused DNS anycast route flapping on the D2S side, resulting in intermittent D2S PO Creation failures.
Resolution: D2S removed the track from the static route, stabilizing the DNS anycast route. Failed requests were repushed and recovered, and the incident was closed after one day without further D2S failures.

Investigation Summary: The scheduled TCB01 package incorrectly changed Chassis Orders from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered". The package behavior was based on SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic involving RF status, which was not appropriate for FDP where RF is disconnected. The corrected TCB01 behavior was validated in UAT1 and deployed to PROD; the package was scheduled and the latest file was processed successfully.
Important Findings: ['TCB01 selected Chassis Orders with status "Shipment Instructed" and RF status "Send Shipment to RF", then changed the order status to "Ordered".', 'In FDP, RF is disconnected, and Chassis Order status must not be updated by the TCB01 file.', 'The agreed TCB01 scope was to update Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date, while preventing status updates.', 'Some UAT1 records were not updated because update_date in column 127 was not today or yesterday; updating update_date to the current date allowed the changes to be reflected.', 'The PROD fix was deployed, the package was scheduled, and the latest TCB01 file was processed successfully after update_date was updated.']
Root Cause: The TCB01 package retained SC Force/SC Force 2.0 logic that updated Chassis Order status from "Shipment Instructed" to "Ordered" based on RF status, although this status update was not valid for FDP.
Resolution: Modified TCB01 processing so that it does not update Chassis Order status and only updates Planned Completion Date and K1_1_OK_Actual_Date. The fix was validated in UAT1, deployed to PROD, and the TCB01 update_date column was set to the current date before processing the latest file.

Ticket key: MFTBCFFR-1337
Ticket Identity
Ticket type: Bug
Ticket Summary: Journal data with a tax rate of 0% is displayed on the screen as a tax rate of 10%.
Ticket Description: ・Confirm with OBC regarding workarounds.
⇒4/21 We will consider measures based on the response from OBC.
===OBC answer===
[1: If it is a tax-exempt transaction]
The cause is that the "tax classification" is not specified.
As a result, the journal entry is likely to be registered under the tax category "Taxable Purchase", which is the initial value of the account.
First of all, in Account Bugyo, you cannot register a journal entry slip with a tax rate of 0% for taxable transactions.
If this is a tax-free transaction, no tax calculation is required, so the tax rate in this case can be said to be 0%.
Therefore, although the account items such as "Parts" attached in this journal entry example are normally taxable transactions,
If you want to register a journal entry as a tax-exempt transaction (=0%) only this time,
Please explicitly set the debit tax classification (CSJS203) to "1", which is the tax classification code for non-taxable purchases.
[2: If the consumption tax amount is recorded separately]
The example journal entry you received is a taxable transaction, but the consumption tax amount is recorded in a separate statement.
If the amount is 0% if the consumption tax amount is not included, then the answer is that there is no problem with the journal entry received.
Even if the consumption tax amount is not included in the statement, the main item will be subject to 10% tax when calculating consumption tax.
The correct state is to display 10%.
============

Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Re-test showed that consumption tax journal entries were still being created for MFTBC PO. The issue was corrected by updating journal creation behavior by order type and MFTBC account status. Tax lines are now included for Body Building Orders, while Modification Orders for MFTBC accounts do not create journals.
Important Findings: ['Re-test failed because consumption tax journal entries were created in MFTBC PO.', 'Body Building Order Non IBOS creates a tax line in the journal.', 'Body Building Order IBOS creates a tax line in the journal.', 'For Modification Orders, MFTBC Account does not create a journal, while Non MFTBC Account creates a journal.']
Root Cause: Journal creation behavior for MFTBC PO did not correctly differentiate Modification Orders by MFTBC Account status.
Resolution: Updated the journal creation logic so that Modification Orders with MFTBC Account create no journal, while Non MFTBC Account Modification Orders create a journal; tax lines remain in journals for Body Building Order Non IBOS and IBOS.

Reported by: Hajime Miyauchi
Created by: Hajime Miyauchi
Watched by: Anubhav Mangal, Hajime Miyauchi
Labelled as : 
Bug Category: Fix Required
Bug Type: KB interface
Track: CS-SV
Affected System: Siebel
Impacted Environments : 
Sprint: FDP KB - Audit
Investigation Report
Investigation Summary: Tax Journal entries were created, but account code mappings were incorrectly configured and some required account codes were missing from journal lines. The account code master initially stored concatenated values such as 25580 instead of separating account and sub-account codes as 255-80. After correcting the master configuration and addressing the remaining missing-code and zero-value journal issues, the incident was confirmed fixed.
Important Findings: ['Tax Journal can be searched using the Job card# in Project code.', 'All expense items require accounting codes if they must be journalized.', 'Account code and Sub-account code must be maintained separately; for example, 255 and 80 must produce 255-80 rather than 25580.', 'For JC# I001215124, account codes 255-80 and 255-03 were initially absent from the required credit and debit journal lines.', 'A 0-yen journal entry was created for recycling fee even though no recycling fee existed.', 'The account code master was corrected and the issue was subsequently fixed.']
Root Cause: Incorrect and incomplete account-code master configuration: account and sub-account codes were stored as concatenated values instead of separated hyphenated values, causing incorrect or missing journal account-code mappings.
Resolution: Corrected the account codes in the master so account and sub-account codes are separated with a hyphen, and fixed the remaining missing account-code and 0-yen journal-entry behavior.
Technical Entities: ['Tax Journal', 'Job card#', 'Project code', 'accounting code', 'Journal', 'Account code', 'Sub-account code', 'account code list', 'account code master', '25580', '255-80', '25504', '255-04', '255-03', 'JC# I001215124', 'automobile tax (environmental performance percentage)', 'automobile tax (classification)', 'recycling fee']
